If anyone sends Gonzaga home early, look at the 3 line. Upset watch: 12 Tennessee St. against 5 Miami. Tennessee St. has won 15 straight. Miami has three bad losses and went out of the ACC tournament in its first game, to a 12-20 Boston College team.

West. Florida State, Texas, Seton Hall, Baylor. The awkward truth is that the West's 2 seed is rated higher than its 1, and its 3 seed is right behind. Texas is fourth in the country at 32.61, Florida State seventh at 29.54, and Seton Hall eighth at 29.08. Texas played the toughest schedule of the top seeds, rated 11.19, and lost to Alabama in the SEC semifinal by six. Also in the West: 8 Wisconsin against 9 Purdue, two Big 10 teams meeting in the first round. Purdue won the regular-season title at 16-4, and Wisconsin finished three games behind. Read nothing into the seeds. 7 Memphis against 10 Yale is the other one to watch: Yale is 30-3, unbeaten in the Ivy League and on a 19-game winning streak. Memphis has zero top-25 wins and a schedule rated 0.09, which is a polite way of saying it hasn't been asked many questions.

Midwest. Florida, Georgetown, Utah St., Kansas State. On paper this is the softest top four, at 108.81, but that's misleading. Kansas State is a weak 4, rated 26th with an average margin of 7.1. Utah St. is the fifth-best team in the country by rating, a 3 seed, and it lost the Mountain West final to the No. 1 overall in overtime by one point. A 2 seed in Georgetown's spot should be nervous, and a 1 seed in Florida's spot should be too. The Midwest also has the best 5 against 12 in the bracket: VCU, 32-1 on a 25-game winning streak, against Navy, 30-3. VCU is a 5 seed because it beat exactly one top-50 team all year. That's fair, and it's also going to make Kansas State's Day 50 extremely unpleasant.

THE FIRST ROUND GAMES TO CIRCLE
VCU against Navy, Day 49. Two mid-majors that lost a combined four games all season. One of them goes home in the first round. Life isn't fair, and neither is the bracket.

Texas Tech against Rutgers. Texas Tech is rated 14th and Rutgers 53rd, but Texas Tech lost by 18 to BYU in its last game, while Rutgers just won four straight in the Big 10 tournament by an average of more than 15.

Marquette against Colorado State. Marquette beat Georgetown and lost to Butler in the Big East tournament. Colorado State won 13 straight before Utah St. stopped it. By rating it's 17.94 to 16.44, and Colorado State has the better recent form.

Ole Miss against UAB. UAB is rated higher, but it lost to a 20-14 UTSA team in the American semifinals. Ole Miss has four top-25 wins and a 28-point loss to Florida. I'm calling it a coin flip, because I don't trust either of them.

WHAT TO EXPECT
The tournament is on neutral courts, so home court is gone. That matters more than it sounds: home teams won 58.8 percent of regular-season games, and conference tournament week showed what happens without them. Scoring dropped to 67.9 points per team from a season average of 69.2. Forty-one games were decided by three points or fewer, and six went to overtime.

Tier S teams went 45-21 in the conference tournaments. That's good, not dominant. Expect the top seeds to win most first-round games and lose a few second-round ones.

And remember the realism ceiling. No game in this league is more than a 99 percent lock, and about one game in 67 is a chaos game where the script goes in the shredder. Over a 67-game tournament, expect roughly one result that makes no sense at all. It might be a 16 seed. It might be your champion. Don't pick it, because you can't, but don't be surprised either.

HOT TAKE
Florida State is the weakest 1 seed and won't reach the Final Four. It's 33-1 and has won 17 straight. It has also played a schedule rated 5.71, the softest of any 1 seed, and its own region contains a higher-rated team in Texas. Florida State's best win in the ACC tournament came against a North Carolina team rated 13th. Texas has beaten better teams more often. I'm taking Texas out of the West.

A HYPOTHETICAL
What if the committee had seeded strictly by rating? The 1 seeds would be San Diego State, Alabama, Gonzaga and Texas. Utah St. would be a 2. Florida and Florida State would both drop to the 2 line. That's not how it works, and it shouldn't be: who you beat matters. But if both Gonzaga and Texas reach the Final Four, the ratings people will be insufferable, and I'll be one of them.

HQ'S BRACKET
Bracketology HQ's entry in the bracket challenge is drafted and goes up as soon as the commissioner gives the nod. My Final Four: San Diego State, Alabama, Texas and Utah St. My champion: San Diego State. It's the chalk pick, and I'm not apologising. The Aztecs are four rating points clear of anyone else, have six top-25 wins and no bad losses, and won their last two games by a combined two points. A team that can win by 49 and by one is a team that can win six in a row. The full writeup will be on the Bracket Challenge page, where you're welcome to beat me. Most of you will. It's been that kind of week.

WHAT'S NEXT
The First Four is Day 48: 11 Bradley against 11 Oklahoma State and 11 Michigan St. against 11 Texas A&M for the last two at-large spots, then 16 UC San Diego against 16 High Point and 16 Oakland against 16 Wagner. Bradley went 28-5 and lost the MVC final to Valparaiso by 19. Oklahoma State got in on the strength of beating teams Arizona couldn't. Settle it on the floor.

Fill in your bracket before Day 48 is played. After that, the only thing left to do is watch, and blame me.

season-3.headline: Week 1: Alabama Starts on Top, North Carolina and Arizona Trip on Opening Week, and Duke Ruins Kentucky's Promotion Party
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Season 3 is three days old, 299 games have been played, and I am already being asked to project a 68-team field. That's like giving someone a film rating after the opening credits. Some teams have played three games, some have played one, and Seton Hall and Illinois haven't played at all. I'm doing it anyway, because that's the job and because last season's résumé of mine needs burying under fresh material.

Ground rules for Week 1. With one to three games per team, the results are a seasoning, not the meal. This field leans on three things: what each team was last season, where the commissioner put it in the offseason tier review, and the handful of results that actually told us something. When those three disagree, I'll say so.

FIRST, THE CORPSE IN THE ROOM
Let's get this over with. My bracket challenge champion last season was San Diego State. San Diego State lost to Ole Miss 76-68 in the round of 32. My Final Four was San Diego State, Alabama, Texas and Utah St. Texas lost to Memphis 88-81 in the round of 32, and Utah St. was beaten 78-67 by Georgetown in the Sweet 16. One out of four. A coin would have done better, and a coin can't read.

The one that got there was Alabama, and Alabama won the whole thing: 70-64 over Georgetown in the final, 38-2 on the season, 92.3 points a game, and a 100-75 Elite Eight demolition of West Virginia for good measure. The Final Four was North Carolina, Alabama, Seton Hall and Georgetown. Seton Hall was a 3 seed and North Carolina a 4, and I had neither of them past the Sweet 16, which tells you everything about my ability to see the future.

Now the receipts I'm keeping. My hot take was that Florida State was the weakest 1 seed and wouldn't reach the Final Four. Florida State lost 76-75 to Wisconsin in the round of 32. My Week 14 line about Ole Miss being "the most dangerous 7 seed I can remember" got mocked after the committee made it an 8, and then Ole Miss knocked out the No. 1 overall seed. So I was wrong about the champion and right about the team that ended him. That's not a good bracket. It is a good column.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: North Carolina, a Final Four team, lost by 14 at New Orleans. Arizona lost at Oakland. Texas Tech lost 79-62 at Illinois–Chicago, a Tier F team, in the biggest upset of the opening week by the numbers. Duke, freshly demoted to Tier A, beat freshly promoted Kentucky 83-79 on a neutral floor. Florida State beat Utah St. 82-75, the best win anybody has.

Not big: almost everything else. Tier S teams went 35-5 and Tier A went 37-7. Most of the top 25 spent the first three days beating teams that will be 9-22 in March by 30. San Diego State's entire season so far is a 96-55 win over Xavier. Gonzaga is 3-0 against Saint Francis (PA), Gardner-Webb and Furman, which is less a schedule than a scrimmage with a ticket price.

THE OFFSEASON, BRIEFLY
The commissioner closed Season 2 with 146 tier changes, and they set the table for this field. Georgetown, Miami, Memphis, BYU and Kentucky moved up to Tier S. Duke, Purdue and UNLV dropped from S to A. Tennessee fell two tiers, from S to B. USC dropped from A to D and promptly lost at home to William & Mary 72-69, which is the kind of loss that makes a demotion feel like a favour. Pacific jumped from C to A after winning the WCC tournament, and San Jose State, Saint Joseph's and American each went up two tiers from D to B.

Early evidence on the tier calls is mixed, which is the polite word. Saint Joseph's beat Oregon 81-80, so that promotion is already paying rent. American lost at home to Northern Colorado by seven, so that one isn't. And Kentucky's first big test as a Tier S team was a loss to Duke, the team that got moved the other way. I'm sure the commissioner found that funny. I did.

THE TOP LINE
Alabama is the No. 1 overall seed and goes East. This isn't about the 86-54 win at Grand Canyon, which proves nothing beyond Alabama being able to find Arizona on a map. It's about the champion coming back as the second-rated team in the country, at 25.43, with the same tier and the same reputation. Until somebody beats it, the crown stays where it is.

San Diego State is the South's 1 seed. It's rated first, at 26.24, and it was rated first for most of last season too. The case against it is the one the bracket made in March: a team that beat everybody by 30 looked mortal the moment the games got tight, and that was before it lost to an 8 seed. A 1 seed, not the overall 1. The Aztecs have to earn that one back.

Texas is the West's 1 seed at 2-0, rated eighth at 24.19. That's a reputation pick, and I'll own it. Texas finished last season rated 32.2, third in the country behind San Diego State and Alabama, and nobody in the SEC besides Alabama has a better recent body of work. Its two wins, over Incarnate Word and Saint Francis (PA), don't count as a body of work.

Florida State takes the Midwest, and yes, I see the irony. I spent March telling everyone it was a fraud, it lost in the round of 32, and now it's the only top-line team with a win that means anything: 82-75 over Utah St. on a neutral court. It's second on the Board at 29.77. When a team does the one thing nobody else has done yet, it gets the line.

The case for Georgetown over Florida State as a 1 is real. Georgetown is the runner-up, now Tier S, and it won 86-75 at New Mexico on Day 3. But beating a top-20 team on a neutral floor beats a road win over the 61st-rated team, so Georgetown leads the 2 line instead, with Gonzaga, Missouri and Michigan St.

MOVERS, OR WHO I'M DOCKING ALREADY
North Carolina goes from the Final Four to a 6 seed in the West. A 77-63 loss at New Orleans is not a small thing. North Carolina was expected to win that game by 21.3 points. It's Tier S and it's rated 23rd, so it stays well inside the field, but you don't open the season by losing by 14 to the Southland and keep your seat at the grown-ups' table.

Texas Tech is a 7 seed in the South. The Red Raiders lost by 17 at Illinois–Chicago in a game they were expected to win by 31.3. Thirty-one. Point. Three. That's the biggest upset of the season by expected margin, and it might stay that way until March. Texas Tech was the 4-ish team in my head before Day 2. Now it's on the 7 line until it gives me a reason not to be.

Arizona is a 7 in the East after a 78-74 loss at Oakland. Last season Arizona sat on the bubble until the committee chose Oklahoma State over it on Selection Sunday, so this is a program with fresh trauma. The rating is still 21.75, 20th in the country, and that keeps it in. Barely a week in, and Arizona is already the team in a horror film that walks into the basement.

Duke is a 6 in the South, which is higher than a freshly demoted Tier A team should be. The 83-79 win over Kentucky is one of the three best results anybody has, and Duke's schedule so far rates 20.86, second in my field only to Nebraska's. Kentucky drops to a 6 in the East. A loss to a good team on a neutral court isn't fatal, but Kentucky was promoted to S partly on faith, and faith just lost by four.

Purdue is out. It's 0-2, it lost 90-65 at Yale and 89-66 at Baylor, and it was demoted from S to A in the offseason. I know Purdue won the Big 10 regular season last year at 16-4. I also know Purdue walked into Week 8 last season and made me look stupid, so this is partly revenge. It's next four out, and it can come back the moment it beats someone.

Baylor is a 3 in the East and is the most complete team of the opening week: 3-0 with wins over Virginia Tech, Hawaii and Purdue, the last by 23. If it beats a top-25 team in the next fortnight, it's on the 2 line.

PATTERNS
The power conferences cleaned up in non-conference play. The ACC went 23-8, the Big 12 went 22-5 and the SEC went 21-7. The Big East was 9-4 and the Big 10 was 14-10, and the Big 10's number would look better if Purdue hadn't been its designated punching bag. At the bottom, the Northeast went 2-17 and the SoCon went 3-13, which is what happens when your league's scheduling philosophy is "take the cheque."

Home teams went 175-122, 58.9 percent, almost exactly last season's regular-season rate of 58.8. Almost every upset in the brief happened on the underdog's floor: New Orleans, Oakland, Illinois–Chicago, Saint Joseph's, Incarnate Word over Notre Dame. If you're a power-conference team booking a road trip to a mid-major gym in November, I hope the money was worth it, because the court isn't.

Scoring sits at 72.0 points per team, up from last season's regular-season average of 69.2. That's three days of data, so don't build a cathedral on it. Close games are everywhere: 46 games decided by three points or fewer and seven overtimes in three days. At the other end, 13 games were decided by 40 or more. Week 1 has a split personality: half coin flips, half public executions.

One more number. Tier D teams went 57-101 and Tier F went 47-97. That's terrible, and it's also better than it sounds, because some of those wins came against power-conference teams, and the realism ceiling means no game in this league is more than a 99 percent lock. Since Season 2 Day 28 about one game in 67 is a chaos game, and over 299 games that's four or five. Texas Tech probably owns one of them. That doesn't get it off the hook, because the committee doesn't grade on excuses.

THE AUTOMATIC BIDS, AND THE ONES I'M GUESSING AT
Nobody has played a conference game, so every automatic bid is a projection of who wins the league tournament in March. The easy ones: Alabama, San Diego State, Gonzaga, Georgetown, Memphis, Florida State and VCU. The Big 10 goes to Michigan St. over Michigan, even though Michigan won at Colorado and has the better schedule so far. Michigan St. has the higher rating, 24.9 to 24.04, and that gap is small enough that I'll change my mind the first time they meet.

The Big 12 is the hard one. Baylor, Kansas, Iowa St., BYU and Kansas State are all Tier S, and Kansas won the conference tournament last year. I'm projecting Baylor, because it's 3-0, it already has the league's best win and Kansas has played one game against Grambling. Ask me again in a week.

A few others worth arguing about. Oakland takes the Horizon at 3-0 with wins over Clemson and Arizona; it was a 16 seed last season, and right now it's a 14. New Orleans gets the Southland on the strength of the North Carolina win, which is one result, but it's a big one. Navy keeps the Patriot League even though it opened with a 64-63 loss at Columbia, a team that finished last season rated minus 22.5. Navy won 30 games last season. I'm giving it one free pass. One. And Wagner, last season's 13-20 bid thief, is 0-3. I wish I could say I'm surprised.

THE BUBBLE
Last four in, the First Four on the 11 line: Creighton against UCLA in the West, and Texas A&M against Colorado State in the Midwest.

Colorado State is the most interesting of the four. It's 3-0, it won 13 straight before Utah St. stopped it last season, and it's rated 49th. Texas A&M was a First Four team last year too, and it's rated 48th after a 76-68 home win over Wright St. that told us nothing. Creighton and UCLA are here because of their tier and league, not because of anything they've done yet: Creighton's best result is a 15-point win at Stony Brook, and UCLA beat Fairfield by only four, 69-65.

First four out: Oregon, Houston, Marquette, UNLV.

Oregon is the closest. It lost 81-80 at Saint Joseph's, which is a good loss by any definition, and it's rated 44th. But Creighton and UCLA haven't lost to anybody, and at this stage that matters. Houston is 1-0 and was promoted to Tier A, but it was rated 3.9 last season, which isn't a tournament team. The promotion is a bet on improvement I want to see before I buy. Marquette hasn't played, beat Georgetown in last season's Big East tournament, and is Tier B. UNLV lost 76-68 at San Diego and was dropped from S to A. It's the most talented team on the bubble and it has played like the least.

Next four out: Purdue, Saint Joseph's, Oklahoma State, St. Louis. Saint Joseph's has the Oregon win and nothing else. St. Louis is 2-0 and gets Kansas and Iowa in the next five days, which means its whole season is about to happen in a week.

HOT TAKE
Duke finishes this season ahead of Kentucky, in the ratings and on the seed list. The commissioner's tier review moved them in opposite directions in the offseason, and their first meeting went the other way. Duke has played the second-toughest schedule in my field so far and beat a Tier S team on neutral ground. Kentucky has wins over Idaho and New Hampshire and one loss to the team the commissioner moved the other way. I'd rather be wrong about this one in public than right about it in private.

A WILD IDEA
What if the committee met today and used only Season 3 results? No tiers, no reputation, just the Board. The 1 seeds would be San Diego State, Florida State, Alabama and Missouri. Michigan, with the toughest schedule of any top-10 team at 16.2, would be a 2. Then it gets weird. Oakland is 73rd on the Board, ahead of TCU and Stanford, so it's on the bubble as an at-large. North Carolina is 45th and Texas Tech is 47th, both clinging on behind Colorado State. Arizona is 44th. Three Tier S teams on the bubble a week into the season. Purdue would be nowhere. That's why the committee looks at more than one week, and it's also why those three teams should be nervous.

HOW THIS FIELD GOES WRONG
Let me save you the trouble of writing in. The 1 line is three-quarters reputation. Florida State is the only top seed with a real win. Seton Hall and Illinois are in the field without playing a game, Seton Hall as a 4 seed because it went to the Final Four and Illinois as a 7 because it's Tier S. If either opens with a loss to a nobody, they'll drop like a stone in a well. I gave Texas Tech, North Carolina and Arizona more benefit of the doubt than their results deserve, and I gave Purdue less. Both decisions will be wrong about half the time. That's Week 1.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 4: Georgetown at Iowa. If Georgetown wins on the road against a Tier A Big 10 team, it moves ahead of Florida State for the last 1 seed.

Day 5: VCU at Utah St. VCU was 32-1 on Selection Sunday last season and was a 5 seed because it beat one top-50 team all year. Here's its chance to beat one in November. Also Arkansas at Houston, which decides whether Houston's promotion was a good idea, and Richmond at Miami.

Day 6: Michigan St. at Kansas, and Kansas State against Michigan. These two decide who leads the Big 10 and the Big 12 in my head. Colorado State goes to Miami the same day, the First Four team's best chance to stop being a First Four team.

Day 7: Texas at Texas Tech. If Texas Tech wins, the Illinois–Chicago loss becomes a fluke. If Texas wins, it gets its first real win as a 1 seed and Texas Tech starts getting nervous about Arizona's company. Also Virginia at Vanderbilt and Kansas at St. Louis.

Day 8: BYU against Gonzaga. Gonzaga's first opponent with a pulse. If Gonzaga wins comfortably, it's knocking on the 1 line. If it loses, the soft schedule talk starts again, and I'll be the one starting it.

WHERE THIS IS HEADED
Seventeen more days of non-conference games, then conference play on Day 21, which is when this field stops being an educated guess and starts being an argument. Alabama is the champion until somebody takes it. San Diego State has to prove March was a blip. Georgetown is one road win from the top line, and North Carolina, Arizona and Texas Tech are one more bad loss from the bubble.

As for me, I start Season 3 with a clean record and a dirty conscience. Bslama for now, and lycka till to anyone who has Texas Tech in a fantasy pool.

season-3.headline: Week 2: Michigan and Virginia Fall Apart, Miami Takes a 1 Seed, and Purdue Proves Me Wrong Again
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Last week I wrote that this field would be wrong about half the time. I was being optimistic. Three of my four First Four teams lost this week, two of them to teams outside the top 100, my 3 seed in the South lost at home by 19 to a Sun Belt team, and my 5 seed in the West lost by 49. Forty-nine. It's Week 2 and the house is already on fire.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Louisiana–Monroe 81, Michigan 62, at Michigan, a game Michigan was expected to win by 29.4. Virginia lost 92-88 at Saint Peter's and then 108-59 at Mississippi State. Georgetown lost 80-76 at Iowa. Seton Hall lost 110-106 in double overtime at East Tennessee State. Utah St. beat VCU by 26 and is now rated second in the country. Kansas beat Michigan St. 78-74.

Not big: San Diego State winning three games by an average of 42 points. Florida going to 5-0 against DePaul, Lamar and friends. Texas, my West 1 seed last week, not playing a single game. It hasn't played since Day 2. You can't lose your seed line if you never leave the house, but you can lose it if everyone around you does something.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State is the No. 1 overall seed and takes over in the East. It's 3-0, rated first at 27.84, and first on the Board at 31.86. It beat Detroit Mercy by 39 and Holy Cross by 46, which is not a résumé so much as a series of crime scenes. But nobody else in the top tier has a good win plus a gap like that, and when the champion is the 13th-rated team in the country, the No. 1 overall has to move.

Yes, Alabama is 13th. It's 2-0 and it won 84-77 at Oakland, which beat Arizona in Week 1, and that's a decent road win. But its rating has slid from 25.43 to 24.19 in two games, because winning by seven at a Horizon team isn't how a defending champion is supposed to look. It keeps a 1 seed and moves to the West. It's on a short lead.

Florida State is 4-0 and holds the South's 1 seed. It's second on the Board, it still owns the best win of the season, 82-75 over Utah St. on a neutral court, and Utah St. made that win look better this week by blowing out VCU. It's also a sign of how the ACC is going that Florida State isn't the conference's highest-rated team any more.

That's Miami, which is the new 1 seed in the Midwest. A 5 seed last week, now 4-0 and rated third at 25.66, up 3.1 points in a week. It beat Gardner-Webb by 60, Richmond by 10 and Colorado State 97-66, and the Colorado State game is the one that matters: it ended Colorado State's place in my field. Two ACC teams on the top line when the league went 19-10 out of conference. I'm aware of the irony. Florida State and Miami are carrying a conference that also lost at Saint Peter's, at Mississippi State, at San Diego and at home to Towson.

Texas drops to the 2 line in the East, and it's not a punishment. It's 2-0 without a game in four days, and Miami played three. The 2 line is Gonzaga, Missouri, Utah St. and Texas. Utah St. is the one I'd fear most: 3-1, rated second in the country at 25.94, its only loss to the 1 seed in its region, and a 96-70 win over a VCU team that was 32-1 on Selection Sunday last year.

GRADING LAST WEEK
I set up five games to watch. Let's see how I read them.

Georgetown at Iowa: I said a Georgetown win would put it ahead of Florida State for a 1 seed. Iowa won 80-76. Then Iowa lost 70-64 at North Florida two days later, which turns Georgetown's loss from respectable into something you mention quietly. Georgetown goes from the top of the 2 line to a 4.

VCU at Utah St.: I called it VCU's chance to beat a top-50 team in November. It lost 96-70. The VCU problem from last season, a great record and nobody beaten, has become a different problem: a bad record and somebody beaten it. VCU drops to a 12, still the A-10 favourite, now in the same spot as the dangerous mid-majors instead of above them.

Arkansas at Houston: I said it would decide whether Houston's promotion to Tier A was a good idea. Arkansas won 80-77 and Houston then beat Tennessee 74-64. Houston is in the field as an 11. I'd call the promotion "probably fine," which is high praise from me in November.

Michigan St. at Kansas and Kansas State against Michigan: I said these would decide who leads the Big 10 and the Big 12 in my head. Kansas won 78-74, so Kansas takes over as the projected Big 12 champion from Baylor. Kansas State beat Michigan 80-75 on a neutral floor, and Michigan's week is a whole section of its own. The Big 10 is still Michigan St.'s, for reasons I'll defend below.

Colorado State at Miami: I said it was Colorado State's chance to stop being a First Four team. It stopped being a First Four team. It's next four out.

One hit, Houston, out of five. At least the games I picked turned out to matter.

MOVERS
Michigan, from a 3 to an 8. The Louisiana–Monroe loss is the biggest upset of the season so far by expected margin, beating Texas Tech's loss at Illinois–Chicago last week. A home loss by 19 to the Sun Belt counts as a bad loss whatever your rating is. Add the neutral-court loss to Kansas State and Michigan is 2-2, rated 26th, with the 90-84 win at Colorado as the only thing keeping it out of the double digits. Michigan's rating fell 5.2 points in a week. Only Virginia fell further.

Virginia, from a 5 to the First Four. Its rating fell 8.7 points, from 16th to 41st. It lost by four at Saint Peter's, which is a forgivable road loss to a decent MAAC team, and then lost by 49 at Mississippi State, which is not forgivable in any league on any planet. Neither loss is to a team outside the top 100, so the Board doesn't count them as bad losses. My eyes do. Virginia keeps a place in the field because it's Tier S and it has two more months to remember how to play defence, and it's one more bad week from leaving altogether.

Seton Hall, from a 4 to a 6. Losing 110-106 in double overtime at East Tennessee State isn't a disaster. It's a road game against a SoCon contender, and Seton Hall scored 106. But it was expected to win by 16.2, and the Final Four team doesn't get to lose that one and keep its line. East Tennessee State, meanwhile, becomes my SoCon champion. Wofford is rated slightly higher, but it lost at Campbell, and East Tennessee State owns arguably the best win any mid-major has this season.

Georgetown, from a 2 to a 4, covered above. Baylor stays on the 3 line, and Kansas moves up beside it. Utah St. goes from a 4 to a 2. Illinois goes from a 7 to a 3: it has played one game, beaten Columbia by 38, and it's rated sixth in the country. That's a lot of seed for one game, and I'll explain it in the hot take, because I don't fully trust it either.

Yale goes from a 12 to a 6. The Bulldogs are 5-0, rated 23rd, and have scored 90 or more in four of five games, including 102 at Hofstra. They beat Purdue by 25. At this point Yale isn't a cute Ivy League story. It's a good team that happens to be in the Ivy League.

THE BUBBLE AND THE BLOODBATH
Three of last week's First Four teams lost, and two of them lost to teams outside the top 100. Creighton lost 67-63 at home to Utah Valley, a 3-3 WAC team, in a game it was expected to win by 22.5. UCLA lost 72-64 at Longwood. Colorado State was beaten by 31 at Miami. Texas A&M didn't lose, and it's out anyway: beating Wright St. by eight and Colgate by four is not a reason to keep anybody.

Last four in, the First Four on the 11 line: Virginia against Purdue in the East, and Syracuse against Saint Joseph's in the West.

Purdue is my favourite thing in this field. Last week I left it out at 0-2 and said it could come back the moment it beat someone. It went 3-0: 81-65 over Ole Miss, 87-76 at Queens, my ASUN champion, and 85-74 over Kennesaw St. Its schedule rates 10.66, one of the toughest of anyone near the bubble. It's back in. Purdue has now proved me wrong in two different seasons, and I'm starting to think it does it on purpose.

Saint Joseph's is 3-0 and beat Oregon. Oregon is rated higher, 49th to 61st, but head-to-head is the cleanest tiebreaker there is, and Saint Joseph's has the win. Syracuse lost 86-81 at San Diego, a bad loss, but it's rated 45th and the other two wins came on the road. Virginia is covered above.

First four out: Texas A&M, Oregon, Mississippi State, San Francisco.

Oregon is 2-1 with a one-point loss at Saint Joseph's and a one-point overtime win over Southern Utah, which is a team I picked to win the WAC and which is now 1-5. We'll come back to that. Mississippi State is the most interesting team on the bubble. It beat Virginia by 49 and lost at home to West Georgia by 10. It's either a tournament team or a team that had one perfect night, and I need more games to tell which. San Francisco is 3-0, rated 55th, and has beaten nobody it shouldn't have.

Next four out: Colorado State, Marquette, UCLA, Creighton. UNLV drops off the board entirely. It's 1-1 with a bad loss at San Diego, and San Diego, at 3-0 with wins over UNLV and Syracuse, is starting to look like this season's bubble executioner.

THE AUTOMATIC BIDS
Five automatic bids change hands this week.

The Big 12 goes from Baylor to Kansas, which beat Michigan St. and has the league's only top-25 win. Baylor is 3-0 and hasn't lost anything. It just hasn't won as much. Baylor plays at Michigan on Day 9 and can take it straight back.

The SoCon goes to East Tennessee State, covered above. The Summit goes from Denver to Kansas City, which is 5-0 and up 4.5 rating points, tied for the biggest rise among top-100 teams, from 108th to 69th. Denver is 3-0 and has done nothing wrong, but Kansas City won at DePaul and beat Troy by 24, and it's rated higher now.

The WAC goes to UT Arlington, 5-0, after beating Norfolk State by 20. My Week 1 pick, Southern Utah, is 1-5. It lost at Virginia, at SMU, at Oregon in overtime and at North Carolina, then came home and lost to Wofford by 15. I have nothing to say in my defence except that its schedule was brutal, and that's not really a defence when you lose the home game too.

The Big 10 stays with Michigan St., and here's why. It's 1-1, and the loss was by four at Kansas. Illinois is rated higher, 25.07 to 24.43, but Illinois has played one game against Columbia. Ohio St. is 4-0 but rated 24th. Michigan St.'s schedule rates 11.67 and Illinois's rates minus 5.53. Until Illinois plays someone with a pulse, Michigan St. keeps the projection, even as a 5 seed.

The ones that held: Navy beat Valparaiso 75-54, which used up its free pass from last week and also hurt my MVC pick. Valparaiso is 1-2 and drops to a 13, still the MVC favourite because nobody else in the league has a rating within 50 places of it. Saint Peter's moves up to a 13 after beating Virginia. New Orleans, the team that beat North Carolina, lost by 14 at St. Bonaventure and drops to the 16 line.

PATTERNS
The Big 12 went 15-3 out of conference this week and 37-8 over two weeks. The SEC went 18-6. The WCC went 11-3, and the strangest line in the brief is the WAC at 15-6. UT Arlington is 5-0, California Baptist is playing 8.4 points above its Tier F rating, and Utah Valley won at Creighton. The WAC had a better week than the Big East. Write that down, because it might never happen again.

At the bottom, the Horizon went 3-11. Oakland is the Horizon's only good team, and it lost to Alabama. The Northeast went 4-11 and the Ohio Valley 4-11.

Home teams went 171-127 this week, 57.4 percent. Over two weeks they're 346-249, 58.2 percent, close to last season's 58.8. But this week flipped last week's pattern. In Week 1 almost every big upset happened on the underdog's floor. This week six of the top eight upsets were won by the road team: Michigan, Creighton, St. John's, Wichita State, Richmond and Temple all lost at home. Home court is still worth something on average. It just didn't stop anyone embarrassing themselves in their own gym.

Nine games went to overtime, up from seven, and scoring is flat at 72.0 per team.

Tier S went 35-7 this week and Tier A went 32-9, slightly worse than last week's 35-5 and 37-7. The big teams are losing a little more as the schedules toughen, which is what's supposed to happen. What's not supposed to happen is a Tier S team losing by 49.

HOT TAKE
Illinois is the best team in the Big 10, and it'll be a 2 seed by the time conference play starts. I've put it on the 3 line after one game, and I know how that looks. But Illinois is rated sixth in the country, ahead of Michigan St., and this early the ratings still carry a chunk of last season in them. Illinois was Tier S last season and stayed Tier S. Michigan has lost twice, Michigan St. lost at Kansas, Ohio St. is rated 24th, and Nebraska has played one game. Somebody has to be the Big 10's best team, and the only one that hasn't lost yet is also the highest-rated. I'm projecting Michigan St. to win the league tournament because that's what the evidence says today. My gut says Illinois wins it.

A WILD IDEA
What if the committee punished teams for not playing? Not a rule anybody would write, but humour me. Texas has played two games in six days. Illinois has played one. Nebraska has played one and lost it. Alabama has played two. Meanwhile Florida, Yale and Kansas City are 5-0. If the committee only trusted teams with three or more games, the 1 seeds would be San Diego State, Florida State, Miami and Gonzaga, and Florida would be on the 2 line with Utah St., Missouri and Baylor. Texas, Alabama, Kansas and Michigan St., all on two games, would slide down the bracket, and Illinois, on one game, would be sweating on the bubble. It's not fair, which is why it's fun. For now, Texas and Alabama hold 1 and 2 seeds on reputation and two games each, and that's the shakiest thing in this bracket.

THE DUKE AND KENTUCKY WATCH
My Week 1 hot take was that Duke finishes ahead of Kentucky. After two weeks, Duke is 3-0 with the head-to-head win, and it's ahead on the Board, 22.43 to 21.77. Kentucky is 4-1 and still rated higher, 19.35 to 16.91. Duke won 114-68 at East Texas A&M and needed everything to beat UNC Asheville 76-71. Kentucky beat Niagara by 34 and scraped past Robert Morris 66-55. I've got Duke a seed line ahead, on the 5 line, with Kentucky on the 6. Call it a lead on points. The fight goes on.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 7: Texas at Texas Tech. This one has been building for two weeks. Texas finally plays someone, on the road, against a team that lost by 17 to a Tier F team and wants to prove it was a fluke. Also Virginia at Vanderbilt, which is Virginia's chance to show the Mississippi State game was a one-off, against a Vanderbilt team that's 4-0. And Kansas at St. Louis.

Day 8: BYU against Gonzaga. The game I flagged last week. Both 4-0. BYU has played nobody and Gonzaga has played less than nobody, so one of them is about to get its first real result.

Day 9: Missouri against Iowa St., two unbeaten teams in my top 13, and Baylor at Michigan. Baylor wants its Big 12 projection back, and Michigan needs a win before people stop calling it a tournament team.

Day 12: Georgetown at LSU, Houston at Pacific, New Mexico State at Purdue and San Francisco at Villanova. That's four bubble-shaped games on one day. Purdue gets a chance to prove me wrong a third time.

WHERE THIS IS HEADED
Two weeks in, the pecking order is San Diego State, then a pack of seven or eight teams that could each be a 1 seed by Christmas. The ACC has two 1 seeds and a team that lost by 49. The Big 10 has no clear leader. The Big 12 has the best non-conference record and Kansas on top, for now. The mid-majors have Yale, Utah St. and whatever San Diego is.

As for me, the running total after two editions: one champion pick that went out in the round of 32, one First Four that collapsed, and one WAC champion that's 1-5. Mashi mushkil. It's November. Ask me again at Christmas.

season-3.headline: Week 3: Gonzaga Takes the No. 1 Overall, Seton Hall Blows Its Way to the Top of the Ratings, and Nine Automatic Bids Change Hands
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Three weeks in and the bracket finally has a shape. It's not the shape I drew, of course. Gonzaga is the No. 1 overall seed, Missouri has replaced Alabama as the SEC's projected champion, and the No. 1 team in the national ratings is Seton Hall, a team that lost to East Tennessee State ten days ago. Nine automatic bids change hands. It's been that kind of week, and next week is worse, because the schedule finally grows teeth.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Gonzaga beat BYU 96-73 on a neutral court and won 95-59 at NC State. Missouri beat Iowa St. 75-69 on a neutral floor. Baylor won 80-73 at Michigan. Texas won 88-86 at Texas Tech, its first real result of the season. Yale lost 76-73 at home to Towson in a game it was expected to win by 25.3. And home teams went 144-153 for the week. More on that, because it's the strangest number of the season.

Not big: Seton Hall beating Presbyterian, Long Island and Oregon State by a combined 176 points. It moved Seton Hall's rating up 6.8 points and to No. 1 in the country, and it tells us almost nothing we didn't know. Also not big: Alabama, which still hasn't played since Day 5.

THE TOP LINE
Gonzaga is the No. 1 overall seed and takes the East. It's 6-0, first on the Board at 33.17 and rated third at 28.4. The BYU game was a 23-point win over a Tier S team on a neutral floor, and the NC State game was a 36-point road win in the ACC. Last week I said Gonzaga had played "less than nobody." It's now played somebody, twice, and destroyed both. I'll take my medicine. The soft-schedule argument isn't dead, because the rest of its résumé is Saint Francis (PA), Gardner-Webb, Furman and Cal Poly. But a team that wins like this when someone finally shows up gets the top line.

Missouri is the South's 1 seed and my projected SEC champion. It's 5-0, second on the Board at 32.98, and its win over Iowa St. is one of the four best results of the season. It's beaten a top-20 team on a neutral floor, it won 87-75 at St. John's, and it's rated fourth. The defending champion is 2-0 and hasn't played in four days. The SEC title projection goes to the team that keeps showing up.

San Diego State is a 1 seed in the West. It's 4-0 and rated second at 28.46, and it's played four games against teams that couldn't beat it with a head start. Fair warning: it plays Texas on Day 13 and Iowa on Day 14. A week from now it'll either be the No. 1 overall again or it'll be off the top line.

Baylor takes the last 1 seed, in the Midwest. It's 5-0 with wins over Virginia Tech, Purdue and, this week, 80-73 at Michigan. Its schedule rates 6.24, the toughest of any team on the top two lines bar Kansas, and nobody else on the 2 line has three wins like that. Baylor was my Big 12 champion in Week 1, lost the projection to Kansas last week and hasn't lost a game in between. I'm keeping Kansas as the Big 12 pick because it owns the league's best win, over Michigan St. But Baylor's résumé is deeper, so Baylor gets the 1 seed and Kansas a 2. They don't meet for weeks, and the committee doesn't care about my projections anyway.

Florida State falls off the top line to a 2. It's 5-0 and still owns the best win of the season, 82-75 over Utah St. But it beat Morgan State this week and nobody else, its rating has slid from 24.25 to 23.45 since Week 1, and it's now 16th. Miami drops further, from a 1 seed to a 3. It's 6-0 and rated tenth, and its best win is over a Colorado State team that just lost at Alcorn State. Last week I said Florida State and Miami were carrying the ACC. This week the ACC needed carrying more than ever and neither of them picked it up.

GRADING LAST WEEK
Texas at Texas Tech: I said Texas would finally play someone. It did and won 88-86 on the road. Texas Tech is 2-2 and slides to a 10. Texas stays a 2.

Virginia at Vanderbilt: I called it Virginia's chance to show the Mississippi State game was a one-off. Virginia won 72-52 and handed Vanderbilt its first loss. It moves from the First Four to a full 11 seed. I'm still not trusting it with anything sharp.

BYU against Gonzaga: covered. BYU has fallen 3.8 rating points, from 20th to 29th, and is an 8 seed.

Missouri against Iowa St. and Baylor at Michigan: both favourites won, and both are now 1 seeds.

Every one of my "games to watch" was won by the better team. That's either good reading or a very boring week. Let's call it good reading.

THE HOME COURT COLLAPSE
Home teams went 144-153 this week, 48.5 percent. In Week 1 they won 58.9 percent and in Week 2, 57.4 percent. Over three weeks they're 490-402, 54.9 percent, still a home edge, but this week it vanished. Look at the upset list. Eight of the ten biggest upsets this week were won by the road team: Towson at Yale, North Florida at Wisconsin, Indiana State at Washington, Liberty at Uconn, California Baptist at St. Mary's and three more. Further down, East Tennessee State won at Oklahoma State and St. Louis won at Iowa.

Is home court dead? No. Three days is a small sample, and 54 games were decided by three points or fewer, a new high for the season, so a lot of these were coin flips that came up tails for the home side. But it's worth noting because the schedule over the next six days is full of power teams going on the road: Georgetown at LSU, Kansas at Kentucky, Baylor at Vanderbilt, Michigan St. at Arizona. If road teams keep winning, some of those will go the wrong way.

AUTOMATIC BIDS: NINE CHANGES
The SEC goes from Alabama to Missouri, covered above.

The Big East goes from Georgetown to Seton Hall. I know: last week I dropped Seton Hall to a 6 for losing at East Tennessee State. But East Tennessee State is now 5-1, won at Oklahoma State this week and looks like a real team, so that loss looks a lot better. And Seton Hall is rated first in the country. Some of that rating is the 176-point week, but it's also 5-1 with road wins at Louisiana and UC San Diego. Georgetown is 3-1 and hasn't played since Day 6. Seton Hall goes from a 6 to a 2, one of the biggest jumps in the field.

The Big 10 goes from Michigan St. to Illinois, and this is my hot take from last week coming true faster than I expected. Illinois is 3-0, rated 11th, and won 84-72 at Coastal Carolina and 95-65 at Duquesne. Michigan St. beat UNC Wilmington. Last week I said Illinois had to play someone with a pulse before I'd move. Coastal Carolina has a pulse. It's faint, but it's there.

The small-conference changes: California Baptist takes the WAC from UT Arlington. California Baptist is 7-2, its rating rose 9.2 points, the biggest rise of the week, from 190th to 81st, and it's playing 17.6 points above its Tier F rating. UT Arlington lost to Nebraska and at Sacramento State. Denver takes the Summit back from Kansas City. Denver is 5-0 and up 3.2 rating points to 64th, ahead of Kansas City at 80th, so last week's switch lasted exactly one edition. Marshall takes the Sun Belt from Coastal Carolina: 5-0, up 5.1 rating points, with wins at Davidson and over Princeton by 27. Longwood takes the Big South from High Point, which lost at home to Portland. Delaware State takes the MEAC from Norfolk State, which lost at home to George Washington and Delaware. Delaware State beat San Francisco by 23. And Massachusetts takes the MAC from Ohio. It's 4-0 and won 74-65 at TCU.

THE BUBBLE
Out this week: Wisconsin, Syracuse and Colorado.

Wisconsin lost 74-63 at home to North Florida, the same North Florida that beat Iowa last week and lost to North Carolina by 44 the next day. North Florida is a Tier F team that has now beaten two Big 10 teams. Wisconsin goes from a 9 seed to the next four out. Syracuse won at Seattle this week, but it has the bad loss at San Diego and a rating that keeps sliding, now 48th. Colorado hasn't played since Day 2. That's a week of not playing, and the field kept moving without it. First four out.

In: Texas A&M, Mississippi State and St. Louis.

Texas A&M is 4-0 and up 3.3 rating points to 39th. It beat Loyola (MD) 86-44 and SMU by 16. Last week I wrote it off for beating Wright St. and Colgate. It's done nothing I asked for, but it's kept winning, the rating has climbed, and that's enough this early. It goes from first four out to an 8 seed.

Last four in, the First Four on the 11 line: Mississippi State against St. Louis in the West, and Oklahoma State against Purdue in the East.

Mississippi State is 4-1. The 108-59 win over Virginia looks better now that Virginia won at Vanderbilt, and the home loss to West Georgia looks a little better now that West Georgia is 4-0. St. Louis is 3-2 and won 73-67 at Iowa this week, the kind of road win that gets you noticed. Its losses are to Kansas and Oklahoma State. Oklahoma State lost at home to East Tennessee State but won at St. Louis and at Wichita State, which gives it two road wins over teams in this conversation. Purdue didn't play this week and has one of the toughest schedules on the bubble at 12.12. It plays New Mexico State on Day 12.

First four out: Colorado, Syracuse, Oregon, San Jose State. Oregon hasn't played since Day 5. San Jose State is 4-0 and beat Queens.

Next four out: Liberty, Fresno State, Wisconsin, UCLA. Liberty won 81-73 at Uconn, which is the best road win anybody on the bubble has, and lost at LSU. It's knocking.

Creighton has fallen off the board altogether. It's 2-3 after losing at Columbia and at Siena this week, and its rating fell 5.0 points, the biggest drop of the week. Two weeks ago it was a First Four team. Now it's a cautionary tale.

THE YALE PROBLEM
Yale was 5-0 and a 6 seed. Then it lost at home to Towson, won 77-76 at Richmond by a point and beat College of Charleston 82-38. Towson is 2-2 and rated 138th, so it's a bad loss on the Board, and Yale drops to a 12. Here's the issue: I can only fit one mid-major automatic bid into the top 11 lines without bumping an at-large team, and this week that's New Mexico State. It's 3-0, rated 24th, 20th on the Board and won 95-73 at Richmond, the same Richmond that Yale beat by a single point. Yale is still a good team. It's now a 12 seed nobody wants to play, which is a worse thing to be for everyone else than for Yale.

PATTERNS
The SEC went 22-4 out of conference this week, the best mark of any league so far, and it's 61-17 over three weeks. The Mountain West went 13-3. The ACC went 18-7, but the ACC's losses keep coming in the worst places. At the bottom, the Northeast went 3-18. It's 9-46 over three weeks, and I'd make a joke here but I think they've suffered enough.

Unbeaten teams went from 74 to 43 this week. Five are 6-0: Gonzaga, Miami, Florida, Saint Joseph's and Kansas City. Denver is 5-0, so the Summit has two unbeaten teams and I've given the bid to the one with fewer wins. That's the ratings talking, and I'll let them.

Tier S went 36-4 this week, its best week yet. Tier A went 31-11, its worst. The gap between the elite and the next group is widening, which makes sense: the S teams are starting to play each other and the A teams are starting to play road games.

HOT TAKE
Missouri is the No. 1 overall seed by Christmas, and Alabama doesn't win the SEC. Alabama has played two games in nine days, it's rated ninth, and its best win is at Oakland. Missouri has played five, beaten a top-20 team on a neutral floor, and is rated fourth. Defending champions get the benefit of the doubt in November. By January, they have to have played. Alabama plays Georgetown on Day 13, and if it loses that, nobody will be calling it the favourite any more.

A WILD IDEA
What if the committee seeded strictly by rating? The No. 1 overall seed would be Seton Hall, a team that lost to East Tennessee State, on the strength of beating Presbyterian by 78. The other 1 seeds would be San Diego State, Gonzaga and Missouri. Baylor would be a 2, Florida State would be a 4, and Alabama would be a 3. The bottom of the bracket would be worse: Michigan, 2-3 with a home loss to Louisiana–Monroe, is rated 26th and would be a 7 seed, with 2-2 Texas Tech on the same line. That's why the committee looks at who you beat. And if anyone tells you the ratings alone should decide the bracket, ask them about Presbyterian.

THE DUKE AND KENTUCKY WATCH
Duke won 80-73 at Louisiana Tech and is 4-0. Kentucky didn't play. Duke leads on the Board, 22.11 to 21.59. Kentucky leads in the ratings, 19.17 to 16.6. Both are 6 seeds now. Kentucky hosts Kansas on Day 14, and that's the result that decides who leads this race at Christmas.

WHAT TO WATCH
This is the biggest week of the season so far. Eighteen games in the next six days involve two top-60 teams.

Day 10: Uconn at Saint Joseph's. Saint Joseph's is 6-0 and won at Pittsburgh this week. A win over Uconn and it's a single-digit seed. Utah St. at Tennessee St. is the other. Tennessee St. is 5-0.

Day 12: Georgetown at LSU, New Mexico State at Purdue, Houston at Pacific and San Francisco at Villanova. Purdue has a chance to prove me wrong for the third time this season, and New Mexico State has a chance to prove Yale should have its seed.

Day 13: San Diego State against Texas. A 1 seed against a 2 seed. If Texas wins, it takes San Diego State's place on the top line. Also Alabama against Georgetown, Kansas at San Jose State and Colorado at Syracuse, the first four out meeting itself.

Day 14: Kansas at Kentucky, Baylor at Vanderbilt, Iowa at San Diego State, LSU at Michigan St. and North Carolina at Villanova. That's five top-60 matchups in one day.

Day 15: Florida against Kansas, Michigan St. at Arizona and Butler at Memphis. Kansas plays three of those games in three days, at San Jose State, at Kentucky and against Florida. If it wins all three, it's a 1 seed. If it loses two, it's a 4.

WHERE THIS IS HEADED
Non-conference play ends on Day 20, and next week is when the bracket gets sorted. Half of my top eight seeds play a top-60 team in the next six days. The ones who win become the 1 seeds the committee will compare everyone else against in March. The ones who lose start the conference season with something to prove.

Running total after three editions: a WAC pick that went 2-7, a Summit pick I've now made twice, and a hot take about Illinois that came true. Bit by bit, inshallah.

season-3.headline: Week 4: Villanova and Penn State Lose to Nobody, Alabama Roars Back, and Tennessee St. Is Real
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Last week I promised you the biggest stretch of the non-conference season, Days 10 to 15. The commissioner played Days 10 to 12. So this edition is the trailer, and the film starts on Day 13 with San Diego State against Texas and Alabama against Georgetown on the same day. Even so, the trailer had plot. Villanova and Penn State lost at home to teams rated 230th and 239th. Tennessee St. beat Utah St. by 15 and is 7-0. New Mexico State went to Purdue and won by 32. And Alabama, which I said last week wouldn't win the SEC, looked like the defending champion for the first time all season.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Big: Alabama A&M 74, Villanova 70, at Villanova, a game Villanova was expected to win by 27. Nicholls State 65, Penn State 55, at Penn State, expected the other way by 24.5. Maine won 81-79 at Iowa St. Tennessee St. 85, Utah St. 70. New Mexico State 94, Purdue 62, at Purdue. Ohio St. went 3-0, including a 78-74 win at Valparaiso, and its rating jumped 4.2 points to ninth in the country.

Not big: San Diego State and Seton Hall, which didn't play at all. San Diego State has played four games in twelve days. Seton Hall hasn't played since Day 9. They're the two highest-rated teams in the country, and right now they're also the two least busy.

THE TOP LINE
Gonzaga stays the No. 1 overall seed in the East. It's 7-0 and won 91-59 at Tennessee Tech, its fifth road or neutral win in seven games. It's first on the Board again, at 32.89. Nobody has been better or more consistently away from home.

Missouri holds the South's 1 seed. It beat Alabama State 76-41 and nothing else, but it's 6-0 with the Iowa St. win and is third on the Board. Missouri is also my projected SEC champion, and that projection is the one I'm least comfortable with this week. More on that in a minute.

San Diego State keeps the West's 1 seed on a technicality: it's rated second at 28.85 and nobody beat it, because nobody played it. It's 4-0 with two road wins, at Detroit Mercy and Abilene Christian, which isn't a road trip so much as a tax write-off. Day 13 against Texas and Day 14 against Iowa will settle whether it stays there.

Baylor holds the Midwest's 1 seed and takes back the Big 12 projection from Kansas. That's the second time that projection has changed hands in four weeks, so take it as seriously as you take a weather forecast. Baylor is 7-0, rated sixth at 25.95, and won 97-65 at Longwood this week. Kansas is 5-0, rated 18th, and beat North Dakota. Kansas still has the better single win, over Michigan St. But Baylor has played seven games and won all of them, and its rating is more than three points higher. Kansas gets its chance to answer in three days: at San Jose State, at Kentucky and against Florida on Days 13 through 15.

THE ALABAMA PROBLEM, OR: MY HOT TAKE IS IN TROUBLE
Last week I wrote that Missouri would be the No. 1 overall seed by Christmas and that Alabama wouldn't win the SEC. Alabama then played three games in three days: 104-40 at North Carolina Central, 87-76 over Providence and 79-66 over Marquette. Its rating jumped from 24.6 to 26.55, from ninth to fifth. It's now rated 0.59 points behind Missouri. It's 5-0, it's won its three road and neutral games, and it's the top 2 seed in the bracket, in the Midwest.

Am I backing off the take? No. But I'm not going to pretend this week didn't happen. Providence and Marquette are not the 1985 Celtics, and the 104-40 game was against a team rated 300-something. Alabama still hasn't beaten anyone rated in the top 50. It plays Georgetown on Day 13 and Northeastern on Day 15. If it beats Georgetown, the take is on life support. If it doesn't, I'll be insufferable.

THE 2 LINE AND THE OHIO ST. QUESTION
The 2 line is Alabama, Seton Hall, Memphis and Ohio St. Ohio St. is the newcomer, up from a 5. It's 7-0, rated ninth, eighth on the Board, and has three road wins, the best at Valparaiso. Here's the uncomfortable part: Ohio St. is now rated higher than Illinois, my projected Big 10 champion, 24.09 to 23.2, and it's ahead on the Board too. I'm keeping Illinois as the projection for one more week, because Illinois has won at Denver, at Coastal Carolina and at Duquesne, and that's three road wins over teams with pulses. But if Ohio St. keeps winning by 30 while Illinois plays once every three days, I'll switch. Hot takes are like milk. They're great until they go off.

Seton Hall drops from the Midwest to the West but stays a 2. It's still rated first. It's still 5-1. It just hasn't done anything for three days, and the 2 line is a crowded room.

GRADING LAST WEEK
I flagged six games played this week.

Uconn at Saint Joseph's: I said a Saint Joseph's win would make it a single-digit seed. Uconn won 75-70. Saint Joseph's stays a 10. Uconn stays a 10 and gets the best road win of its season.

Utah St. at Tennessee St.: I said Tennessee St. was 5-0. Now it's 7-0, and it beat Utah St. by 15. See below.

Georgetown at LSU: Georgetown won 61-57, its first good win since losing at Iowa. Georgetown stays a 4.

New Mexico State at Purdue: I said Purdue had a chance to prove me wrong for the third time. It had the chance, and New Mexico State won by 32. Purdue is 3-3 and out of the field. I've been arguing with Purdue for two seasons and I finally win one, on a night Purdue would rather forget.

Houston at Pacific: Houston won 76-62. Pacific drops from a 7 to a 9.

San Francisco at Villanova: Villanova won 84-69. That's its only good news of the week.

TENNESSEE ST. IS REAL
Tennessee St. is 7-0, rated 33rd, and up 5.0 rating points this week, from 56th. It beat Utah St., a Tier S team rated 13th, by 15 points at home, and then beat Coppin State 86-44. Last season it was a 12 seed that had won 15 straight. Its Board score of 20.5 is better than Kentucky's.

It's still on the 12 line, and I want to explain why, because it looks wrong. I can fit only one mid-major champion onto the first 11 lines without pushing an at-large team below a First Four team, and New Mexico State has the better résumé: 4-0, rated 17th, 16th on the Board, and a 32-point win at a Big 10 school. So Tennessee St. is the best 12 seed in this bracket, and no 5 seed wants it.

MOVERS
Out: Villanova, Penn State, Purdue, St. Louis and Oklahoma State.

Villanova was a 7 seed. Then it lost at Boise State and at home to Alabama A&M, and now it has two bad losses. It won at Wofford and beat San Francisco, but two losses to teams outside the top 100 in three days is how bubble teams are born. First four out.

Penn State was a 9. It lost by 10 at home to Nicholls State, a Southland team, and its schedule rates minus 8.17, the softest of anybody near the field. Next four out. St. Louis lost 96-77 at New Haven, a 2-5 team, and falls off the board entirely. Oklahoma State lost at home to Navy, 69-59.

In: Colorado, Fresno State, Liberty, Oregon and Syracuse.

Colorado jumps from first four out to a 7 seed. It's 3-1 after beating Bradley by 27 and Georgia by 32, and Georgia was 5-0. Its rating rose 3.5 points to 25th. One confession: Colorado has played four games, all at home. It's the only team in my field without a single road or neutral game. It goes to Syracuse on Day 13 and Florida on Day 18, and we'll find out whether this team travels.

Fresno State is 5-1, rated 42nd, and 39th on the Board. It beat California and UNC Asheville this week, and its one loss was at Wofford in Week 1. It goes from next four out to a 9. Oregon won 91-62 at Loyola (MD), is 3-1 with its only loss by a point at Saint Joseph's, and gets a full 11. Syracuse is 5-1 and won at UTEP by 27. Liberty didn't play, but it owns a road win at Uconn, and Uconn just won at Saint Joseph's.

Last four in, the First Four on the 11 line: Mississippi State against Liberty in the Midwest, and Syracuse against Texas Tech in the East.

Mississippi State is the strangest résumé in the field. It beat Virginia by 49, it's rated 36th, and it now has two bad losses, to West Georgia and, this week, 73-72 in overtime at Hawaii. Texas Tech is 5-2, and it went 3-0 this week, but its rating fell 4.5 points, from 28th to 50th, because it beat Murray State, South Florida and Drake by less than it was supposed to. Winning and sinking at the same time is a special talent.

First four out: Villanova, San Jose State, Purdue, Ole Miss. Next four out: Penn State, Oklahoma State, Providence, UCF.

Elsewhere: Iowa St. drops from a 5 to a 6 after the Maine loss. Maine then lost 68-67 at Eastern Kentucky, a 1-4 team rated 343rd, which tells you everything about this sport. Utah St. drops from a 4 to a 5. Kentucky drops from a 6 to a 7.

THE AUTOMATIC BIDS
Five change hands, and three of them are teams coming back.

The Big 12 goes back to Baylor, covered above. The MAC goes back to Ohio after Massachusetts lost at home to High Point and San Diego. The Big South goes back to High Point, the team that beat Massachusetts, after Longwood lost to Baylor and at Oregon State and fell to 4-5. Rotating these projections every week is starting to feel less like analysis and more like musical chairs.

The two new ones: Nicholls State takes the Southland. It's 4-0 and won at Penn State, and New Orleans, my pick since Week 1, is 2-4. Alcorn State takes the SWAC: 4-1, with wins over South Carolina, Colorado State and at Cincinnati. That's the best résumé in the league, and Arkansas–Pine Bluff, my pick since Week 1, is 3-3.

PATTERNS
Scoring is falling. Teams averaged 72.0 points in each of the first two weeks, 70.7 in Week 3 and 68.9 this week. That's three points in two weeks. Last season the regular-season average was 69.2, so the league is drifting back toward normal as the schedules toughen and the 40-point blowouts thin out. There were nine games decided by 40 or more this week, the fewest yet.

Home court came back, partly: 161-138, 53.8 percent, after last week's 48.5. Over four weeks it's 651-540, 54.7 percent. Close games keep piling up, 52 decided by three points or fewer.

Tier S went 27-2 this week. That's 93 percent, its best yet, and the two losses were Utah St. at Tennessee St. and Iowa St. against Maine. The elite are beating everyone they're supposed to, which is why the bracket's top four lines barely moved while the 7 to 11 lines turned over.

The Big 12 went 18-7 out of conference and the Big 10 18-8. At the bottom, the Big South went 2-14. Its best team, High Point, is my projected champion and is rated 108th. The Patriot went 4-14, which puts Navy's road win at Oklahoma State in perspective: it's the best win in that league by a mile.

HOT TAKE
Tennessee St. finishes non-conference play unbeaten and ends up on the 7 line or better by Selection Sunday, as an automatic qualifier the committee can't bury. Its next real test is California Baptist on Day 17, a 10-2 team playing 20.9 points above its tier. If Tennessee St. wins that, it'll be 9-0 or 10-0 going into Ohio Valley play, in a league it should win by four games. The committee loves a team that wins every game and beats a Tier S team by 15. It just won't admit it until March.

A WILD IDEA
What if the committee only counted road and neutral games? Duke would be the darling: 4-0 away from home. Texas is 4-0 away, with wins at Texas Tech, Western Kentucky, Southeast Missouri State and Army. Memphis is 4-0 away and has played one home game all season. Gonzaga is 5-0 away. Colorado, the team I just moved up to a 7, would have no résumé at all. It's played zero road games. Seton Hall would be 2-1, with the East Tennessee State loss counting double. The real committee doesn't work that way, but it does look at road records, and this season's home court collapse in Week 3 suggests it should look hard.

THE DUKE AND KENTUCKY WATCH
Duke beat Tarleton State 79-41 and is 5-0. Kentucky won 81-75 at New Orleans and is 5-1. In the ratings, Kentucky's lead has shrunk to 17.57 against 17.15, the closest it's been. On the Board, Duke leads 21.92 to 20.25. Duke is a 6 and Kentucky a 7. The Week 1 take is winning on points and closing in on the knockout. Kentucky hosts Kansas on Day 14 and Duke goes to Texas on Day 18, so both get a big result before Christmas.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 13: San Diego State against Texas, and Alabama against Georgetown. Two games, two seed lines decided. If Texas wins, it takes San Diego State's 1 seed. If Georgetown wins, my hot take lives. Also Colorado at Syracuse, Colorado's first road game, against a First Four team.

Day 14: Kansas at Kentucky, Baylor at Vanderbilt, Iowa at San Diego State, LSU at Michigan St., North Carolina at Villanova and Iowa St. at New Hampshire. Villanova needs that one badly.

Day 15: Florida against Kansas, Butler at Memphis and Michigan St. at Arizona. Butler is 5-0. Memphis has played one home game.

Days 16 to 18: Virginia at Seton Hall, Michigan at Georgetown, Texas A&M at Michigan St., West Virginia at Nebraska, California Baptist at Tennessee St., Colorado at Florida, Duke at Texas and Arizona at Yale. If you play all six days, I'll need a bigger notebook.

WHERE THIS IS HEADED
Eight days of non-conference play left. The top of the bracket is settled into a group of about eight teams, and the next six days will sort them. The bottom of the field is chaos: five teams out this week, five in, and the last four in have a combined four bad losses. That's normal for December. It won't be normal by February.

Running total: Purdue finally loses an argument to me, three auto bid projections go back to teams I'd already dropped, and my Alabama take survives by a thread. Yalla, Day 13.

season-3.headline: Week 5: San Diego State Leaves Orbit, Kansas Takes the Big 12 Back, and Duke Knocks Out Kentucky
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ, where I'm holding a small funeral. Last week I said that if Alabama beat Georgetown, my hot take was on life support. Alabama won 76-75. The take has been unplugged, the family has been notified, and I'm wearing black. Moving on.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
San Diego State beat Texas 85-76 on a neutral floor and then beat Iowa 95-40. Kansas played three games in three days against real teams and won all three. Penn beat Houston. Maine beat Miami. Kentucky got beaten by 27 on its own floor. And for once, all of it mattered.

SAN DIEGO STATE IS IN ITS OWN POSTCODE
The Aztecs are the No. 1 overall seed again, and it isn't close. Their rating jumped 5.9 points in a week to 34.79. The second-best team in the country is Seton Hall at 30.94, and nobody else is above 29. On the Board, San Diego State is at 40.33 and Alabama is second at 34.44. That's the gap between first and second. It's also roughly the gap between second and 13th.

The Iowa game was a 55-point win over a Big 10 team that was in my field last week. It's still in my field this week, as a First Four team, which tells you how forgiving December is. Iowa's best win is over Georgetown. Iowa's worst loss is a war crime.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State (East), Alabama (South), Kansas (West) and Gonzaga (Midwest).

Alabama is 8-0, second on the Board, and my projected SEC champion again, two weeks after I took the projection away from it. Missouri drops from a 1 seed to a 3. It played one game this week, a 75-67 win at Rhode Island, and its rating has slid to ninth. Missouri didn't do anything wrong. It just didn't do anything.

Kansas is the story of the week. At San Jose State, 78-62. At Kentucky, 86-59. Florida on a neutral floor, 84-72. Kansas is 8-0 with two top-25 wins and two more over top-50 teams, the best collection in the country, and it takes back the Big 12 projection from Baylor. That's the third time that projection has moved. I've changed the Big 12 champion more often than I've changed my bedsheets, and I'm not proud of either number.

Baylor lost 73-68 at Vanderbilt and drops from a 1 to a 4. Its rating fell from sixth to 14th. Vanderbilt is 8-1 and a 7 seed, and if you'd told me in Week 1 that Vanderbilt would be the team ending unbeaten seasons, I'd have asked what you were drinking.

Gonzaga holds the last 1 seed at 8-0. It played once this week and beat Canisius 90-35. Seton Hall and Florida State are the closest challengers. Seton Hall is rated second and has zero wins over top-50 teams, which makes it the best team in the country that's never beaten anybody.

THE KNOCKOUT
In Week 1 I wrote that Duke would finish this season ahead of Kentucky. The commissioner had just promoted Kentucky to Tier S and demoted Duke to Tier A, and Duke had just beaten Kentucky by four. Five weeks later: Duke is 8-0, rated 24th, and a 6 seed. Kentucky is 6-2, rated 49th after the 27-point home loss to Kansas, and a 10 seed. On the Board, Duke leads 23.95 to 14.25.

The ref has stopped it. Duke wins by knockout in the fifth round. I'd like this result framed and hung in the commissioner's office, next to the offseason tier review.

COLORADO GOT ITS PASSPORT
Last week I pointed out that Colorado was the only team in my field that hadn't played a road game. This week it played three: 82-69 at Syracuse, 90-62 at Georgia Tech and 96-75 at Pittsburgh. Its rating rose 4.1 points to 16th, and it goes from a 7 to a 4. I asked whether this team travels. It travels like a man who's just discovered budget airlines.

THE PENN GAME
Penn won 69-65 at Houston. Houston was expected to win by 34.6 points. That's the biggest upset of the season by a distance, beating Louisiana–Monroe over Michigan by more than five points. Penn is 4-8 and rated 331st. It lost to Liberty by 15 the next day, just to prove the Houston game wasn't a sign of anything.

Houston played one game this week. It lost that game. It was an 8 seed and now it's first four out, which is the bracketology equivalent of going out for milk and coming home divorced.

MOVERS
Arizona goes from a 5 to a 2 after beating Michigan St. 90-52. Michigan St. falls from a 5 to a 7 and its rating dropped 4.0 points. Kentucky drops from a 7 to a 10. Utah St. lost at Stanford and slides to a 7. Miami lost at Maine and drops from a 4 to a 5.

Out: Houston, Liberty, Syracuse and Texas Tech. Liberty lost at home to Bethune-Cookman and Kansas City in the same week. Syracuse lost to Colorado, which is fine, but it was on the First Four line and fine wasn't enough. Texas Tech is out of the field for the first time this season, and its rating is 58th, which for a Tier S team is like a five-star hotel with a two-star review that just says "bees."

In: San Jose State, Ole Miss, Providence and UCLA.

Last four in: Providence against Pacific, and Iowa against UCLA. Pacific lost at SIU Edwardsville, a 1-7 team. Iowa lost by 55. UCLA's schedule rates minus 7.38, the softest of any at-large team. Providence is 7-2 and the only one of the four that didn't embarrass itself recently, so naturally it's the one I'm least sure about.

First four out: Houston, Syracuse, Texas Tech, Purdue. Next four out: Villanova, Pittsburgh, Boston College, Liberty.

THE AUTOMATIC BID CAROUSEL
Five change this week. The SEC goes to Alabama and the Big 12 to Kansas, covered above.

Maine takes the America East from New Hampshire, which is 5-6. Maine is 9-4 and has wins over Iowa St. and Miami, two top-25 teams. That's as many top-25 wins as Kansas. It's more than Gonzaga, Seton Hall and Missouri have combined. It also lost to Eastern Kentucky, rated 319th. Maine is the most chaotic résumé in the country and I love it like a dog that eats furniture.

South Carolina Upstate takes the Big South after High Point lost at home to Houston Christian. That's the third straight week I've changed the Big South pick: High Point, Longwood, High Point again, now South Carolina Upstate. The Big South isn't a conference. It's a raffle. East Texas A&M takes the Southland after Nicholls State lost 57-45 at home to Georgia Southern, a 2-6 team.

PATTERNS
Home court came roaring back: 179-117 this week, 60.5 percent, the best rate of the season. Scoring fell again, to 68.7 points per team, the lowest week yet. Tier S went 33-8, its worst week, mostly because the S teams are finally playing each other. The WCC went 4-12 out of conference this week. Gonzaga is carrying that league like a man carrying a sofa up five flights of stairs by himself.

HOT TAKE
Duke beats San Diego State on Day 19. Duke is 8-0, it's at home, and home teams just won 60.5 percent of their games. San Diego State has to play at Duke the day after Duke plays at Texas, which sounds bad for Duke until you notice it means Duke will be the one who's warmed up. I'm not saying it's likely. I'm saying it's the first game this season where I'd take the underdog with my own money, and my own money is all I have left after this season of picks.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 16: Virginia at Seton Hall. Seton Hall's chance to beat literally anyone good.

Day 17: California Baptist at Tennessee St. Two mid-majors that have lost two games between them. Also West Virginia, 8-0, at Nebraska.

Day 18: Duke at Texas, Colorado at Florida and Arizona at Yale. Yale is 11-1 and has played nobody. Arizona is nobody's idea of nobody.

Day 19: San Diego State at Duke. See above. I'll either look like a genius or need a new name.

Day 20: Florida State at Memphis, two unbeaten teams on the 2 line. The winner probably gets a 1 seed.

Day 21: conference play starts, and it starts loud. LSU at Alabama, Mississippi State at Missouri, Arkansas at Vanderbilt, Uconn at Seton Hall and BYU at West Virginia. Non-conference season ends with a bang and conference season starts with another one.

Five editions in, the scoreboard: Duke over Kentucky, landed. Illinois in the Big 10, holding. Alabama not winning the SEC, deceased. Allah yarhamha. Next week, the Aztecs go to Durham.

season-3.headline: Week 6: Seton Hall Still Can't Beat Anybody, Ohio St. Takes the Big 10, and Duke Arrives Warmed Up and Soaking Wet
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Last week I picked Duke to beat San Diego State on Day 19, partly because Duke would be "warmed up" from its game at Texas on Day 18. Duke went to Texas and lost 86-63. It's warmed up the way a car is warmed up after you've driven it into a lake. The Aztecs game is still to come. My confidence has left the building and taken the furniture with it.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Seton Hall lost at home to Virginia. Memphis lost at Cal State Northridge. Tennessee St. lost at home to a 3-6 Air Force team the day after beating California Baptist by 26. Nebraska beat West Virginia by 31. Oregon won at Florida. Twelve teams are still unbeaten, and non-conference play has two days left before the real thing starts.

THE TOP LINE
Same four as last week: San Diego State (East), Alabama (South), Gonzaga (West) and Kansas (Midwest). They went a combined 6-0 this week by an average of 38.5 points. Gonzaga beat Campbell 97-41. Alabama won 103-59 at Wichita State. San Diego State beat TCU by 23 and is still rated 34.74, more than two points clear of anyone. These four aren't playing basketball. They're conducting performance reviews.

SETON HALL: THE BEST TEAM THAT HAS BEATEN NOBODY
Last week I said Virginia at Seton Hall was "Seton Hall's chance to beat literally anyone good." Seton Hall did not take that chance. Virginia won 76-70 in a game Seton Hall was expected to win by 21.5. Seton Hall is still rated second in the country at 32.66. It's also 7-2 with zero wins over top-50 teams. Its two losses are to East Tennessee State and Virginia. Its biggest win is over Louisiana.

So here's my compromise. The rating says Seton Hall is elite. The résumé says Seton Hall is a rumour. I've split the difference and dropped it from a 2 seed to a 3. Uconn plays it twice in two days, Day 21 at Seton Hall and Day 22 at Uconn, which is either a coincidence or the commissioner's idea of an intervention.

OHIO ST. GETS THE BIG 10
For three weeks I've kept Illinois as my Big 10 champion, mostly out of loyalty to a hot take from Week 2. I said I'd switch if Ohio St. kept winning by 30. Ohio St. is 10-0, beat Appalachian State 95-37 this week, and its rating is up to fifth in the country at 28.57. Illinois is 9-0 and rated 12th. I am a man of my word, occasionally. Ohio St. gets the Big 10 projection and a 2 seed. Illinois is a 3, and my Week 2 take gets a dignified retirement rather than a funeral.

THE MID-MAJOR LOGJAM
VCU is the hottest team nobody talks about: 9-1, up 5.1 rating points to eighth in the country, and it beat Massachusetts 93-34 this week. It's a 3 seed. VCU's only loss was by 26 at Utah St. back in Week 2, and since then it has won eight straight, mostly by enough to make the opponent's parents leave early.

That creates a problem for New Mexico State. It's 9-0 and rated 13th, and I can only fit one mid-major champion onto the first 11 lines without pushing an at-large team below a First Four team. VCU's résumé is better, so New Mexico State drops from a 4 to a 12. A 9-0 team rated 13th in the country is a 12 seed in my bracket. That's not me being unfair to New Mexico State. That's me being unfair to whichever 5 seed draws it. I've had a lot of good 12 seeds this season, Yale, Tennessee St. and now this, and this is the one I'd least like to see if I were a 5.

Tennessee St. stays a 12 after the Air Force loss. Air Force was expected to lose that game by 25.3 points, the biggest upset of the week. My hot take that Tennessee St. would finish non-conference play unbeaten died two days before the finish line. I've stopped holding funerals. I'm just keeping a list.

MOVERS
Nebraska jumps from a 7 to a 4. It's 7-1, up 5.0 rating points to 14th, and it beat West Virginia 84-53 to end the Mountaineers' unbeaten run. West Virginia drops from a 6 to a 7. Duke drops from a 6 to a 7 after the Texas game. Texas stays on the 2 line with the 23-point statement it badly needed.

San Jose State rises from a 10 to a 6. Its rating jumped 6.5 points, the most of any team in the top 100, from 48th to 25th, helped by an 84-46 win at UAB. It's the third Mountain West team in my top 24, alongside San Diego State and Utah St., and that's before Fresno State, which is an 8-1 team on the 7 line.

Florida moves up from a 5 to a 4 despite losing at home to Oregon, because it beat Colorado 84-83 the next day. Oregon jumps from an 8 to a 7.

Memphis drops from a 2 to a 3. Losing 71-70 at Cal State Northridge isn't a disaster, but it was expected to win by 19.5, and Cal State Northridge becomes my Big West champion on the strength of it.

THE BUBBLE
Out: Michigan, UCLA and Pacific. Michigan lost 105-73 at Georgetown and its rating fell 6.3 points, from 30th to 61st, the biggest drop in the country. It's Tier S and it's 5-4 and it's out. UCLA lost 70-54 to Uconn on a neutral floor and fell to 89th. Pacific beat Southern Utah, but it still has the bad loss at SIU Edwardsville, and the field moved past it.

In: St. Louis, Boston College and Villanova.

Last four in: St. Louis against Iowa, and Boston College against Villanova.

St. Louis is 6-3 and up 4.2 rating points to 39th. It won 78-43 at Portland State. Iowa didn't play this week, which, after losing by 55 to San Diego State, is the most sensible thing it's done all month. Boston College is 8-0 and has played nobody. It won 83-82 at Jacksonville, and that's its best result. Villanova is 7-3 and still carries those two bad losses from Week 4, but it's won its last two and is rated 41st.

First four out: Pacific, Marquette, Syracuse, UCLA. Next four out: Michigan, Purdue, Houston, Virginia Tech.

AUTOMATIC BIDS
Four change. The Big 10 goes to Ohio St. The Big West goes to Cal State Northridge, covered above. UC Irvine, my pick since Week 1, lost three straight at home this week, to Texas A&M, Wright St. and Samford, and I'd like to formally end that relationship. The SWAC goes to Bethune-Cookman, which is 7-1 and won at Liberty in Week 5. Alcorn State, last week's pick, lost by 40 at Miami and then at Incarnate Word.
