So the Southland goes to Incarnate Word, mostly because the team that beat my SWAC pick seemed like the right replacement for my Southland pick. Is that analysis? No. Is it any worse than what I've done in the Southland all season? Also no.

PATTERNS
Scoring fell for the fourth straight week, to 67.7 points per team. In Week 1 it was 72.0. Teams are scoring four fewer points a game than they did a month ago, which is either better defence or everyone getting tired. Home teams won 59.1 percent. The Big 10 went 21-6 out of conference, its best week yet, and the Northeast went 3-15, which is just the Northeast being the Northeast.

HOT TAKE
Alabama beats Missouri by double digits on Day 22, and Missouri, 9-0 and a 4 seed, loses twice in its first three SEC games. Missouri's rating has fallen from fourth to 19th in two weeks. It's unbeaten because it's played Buffalo, Rhode Island and South Dakota State, and it beat South Dakota State by only six. Missouri gets Mississippi State on Day 21 and Alabama on Day 22. Missouri's unbeaten record is a sandcastle and the tide is coming in.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 19: San Diego State at Duke. My hot take from last week. I'm not withdrawing it. I'm just looking for my coat.

Day 20: Florida State at Memphis, the game that decides who's the best 2 seed. Also St. Louis at Missouri, the First Four team's shot at an unbeaten.

Day 21, conference play starts: LSU at Alabama, Mississippi State at Missouri, Arkansas at Vanderbilt, Virginia at Miami, Uconn at Seton Hall and BYU at West Virginia.

Day 22: Missouri at Alabama, Texas at Florida, Fresno State at San Diego State, Florida State at Virginia and Iowa St. at Arizona.

Six weeks in, the list: Duke over Kentucky, landed. Illinois in the Big 10, retired. Alabama not winning the SEC, deceased. Tennessee St. unbeaten, deceased. Duke over San Diego State, in intensive care. Wish it well. Ya rabb.

season-3.headline: Week 7: Duke Loses by One, LSU Stuns Alabama, and the Mid-Majors Finally Get Seeded Like Adults
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Housekeeping first. HQ no longer files an AP ballot. It turns out my ballot had been quietly replacing the commissioner's every week, like a lodger who redecorates your living room while you're at work. The commissioner's real ballots are back where they belong, and I've been relieved of my vote. I accept this with grace, mostly because my ballot had Missouri second in Week 4.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
San Diego State won 82-81 at Duke. LSU won 72-71 at Alabama. Florida State won at Memphis. Conference play started on Day 21, and the first big conference game of the season ended with the defending champion losing at home to a team I had on the 11 line.

THE DUKE GAME
Last week my hot take was in intensive care. It has now passed away, by one point, in Durham, surrounded by family. Duke lost 82-81 to the No. 1 overall seed after losing at Texas by 23 the day before. I said Duke would be "warmed up." It was warm. It just wasn't enough. One point. Of all the ways for a hot take to die, losing by one is the cruellest, because for about 39 minutes I was a genius.

San Diego State is 11-0 and still the No. 1 overall seed in the East. Its rating actually dipped, from 34.74 to 33.01, because winning by one at Duke counts for less than winning by 35 at Southern Utah. That's ratings logic. It's not mine.

THE TOP LINE
San Diego State, Gonzaga (South), Kansas (West) and Florida State (Midwest).

Florida State replaces Alabama. It's 11-0, it won 70-58 at Memphis this week, and it owns wins over Utah St. and Memphis. Gonzaga is 11-0 and beat South Alabama by 36 and Seattle by 29 this week. Kansas is 11-0 with two top-25 wins and two more over top-50 teams, still the best collection in the country.

Alabama drops to a 2. LSU was expected to lose by 23.8 points and won by one, at Alabama, in the first conference game of its season. Alabama is 10-1 and still fourth in the ratings, but a home loss to an 11 seed costs you the top line in December. Missouri goes to Alabama on Day 22, so we'll know quickly whether this was a blip or a trend.

SETON HALL: NOW RATED NO. 1, STILL HASN'T BEATEN ANYBODY
Seton Hall beat Montana State 116-62 and Uconn 83-57 this week. Its rating rose to 34.95, which is now higher than San Diego State's. It is rated the best team in the country. It also has zero wins over top-50 teams and two losses, to East Tennessee State and Virginia.

I've moved it up from a 3 to a 2, because Uconn is at least a tournament team and 26 points is a margin. But the next three days are the real test. Seton Hall plays at Uconn on Day 22, against Butler on Day 23 and at Georgetown on Day 24. Three games, three days, three teams with a pulse. If it wins all three, I'll stop making this joke. I won't enjoy it.

THE NEW SEEDING RULE
The commissioner has pointed out something I should have done weeks ago: there's no rule that says a mid-major champion can't be seeded above an at-large team. For six weeks I'd been parking strong mid-majors on the 12 line to keep every at-large team above them. That was nonsense. So here's every team where it belongs.

New Mexico State is 11-0, rated 20th, and it's a 5 seed. Northeastern is 10-1, won 77-61 at Houston this week, and is a 6. Tennessee St. is an 8. East Tennessee State, 12-1 and the first team to beat Seton Hall, is a 9, and so is Yale.

That pushes at-large teams down. Virginia is a 12. Uconn, Dayton and Mississippi State are 13s. Texas A&M is a 14. An SEC school is on the 14 line of my bracket next to California Baptist, and nobody has died. The last four in are still the four weakest at-large teams, and they still play the First Four on the 11 line. An 11 seed sounds better than a 14, until you remember it comes with an extra game and a Tuesday night flight to Dayton.

KENTUCKY: THE EPILOGUE
In Week 1 I wrote that Duke would finish ahead of Kentucky. Last week I declared a knockout. This week Kentucky lost 70-67 at Georgia and is out of the field. It's 8-3, rated 63rd, and first four out. Duke, for all its heartbreak this week, is an 8 seed. I'd stop talking about this, but it's the only hot take I've landed all season, so I'm going to keep mentioning it until the commissioner asks me to stop. Possibly after.

MOVERS
Iowa St. jumps from a 5 to a 3. It's up 6.7 rating points to eighth in the country after beating Grand Canyon by 50, North Carolina A&T by 50 and Oklahoma State by 34. That's a team taking out a week of anger on people who did nothing to deserve it.

Boston College is 11-0, up 6.8 rating points, and won 81-62 at Syracuse. It goes from the First Four to an 8. I still don't believe it. More below.

Arkansas lost 77-70 at Vanderbilt and drops from an 8 to a 10. Vanderbilt has now ended two unbeaten seasons, Baylor's and Arkansas's. It's an assassin wearing a 9 seed.

Houston lost 78-61 at Detroit Mercy, a 2-9 team, and then lost at home to Northeastern. Houston was an 8 seed three weeks ago. It's now rated 95th and nowhere near the bubble. Houston's season is a house that fell down while I was describing the curtains.

Out: Kentucky. In: Florida Atlantic, 7-4 with no bad losses and a schedule rated 4.2, the kind of team the committee likes in a room full of teams that have lost to Detroit Mercy.

Last four in: Villanova against Florida Atlantic, and Ole Miss against Providence. First four out: Kentucky, Iowa, Liberty, Louisiana. Next four out: Coastal Carolina, New Mexico, Michigan, Oklahoma State.

AUTOMATIC BIDS
Three change. Southern Illinois takes the MVC from Valparaiso. It's 10-1, rated 44th, one spot behind Valparaiso, and it hosts Valparaiso on Day 23. I'm picking the team with three more wins. Hawaii takes the Big West from Cal State Northridge, which lost twice this week. Norfolk State takes the MEAC from Delaware State, which lost at home to Radford in double overtime. Every week I change three or four of these, and every week a 16 seed somewhere feels a cold wind.

PATTERNS
Sixty-one games this week were decided by three points or fewer, the most of the season. San Diego State by one, LSU by one, Texas by two in overtime at New Orleans. Conference play adds familiarity, and familiarity breeds coin flips. Home teams won 59.5 percent. The Big 10 went 16-3 out of conference and Conference USA went 9-0. Scoring held at 67.7 per team, matching the season low.

HOT TAKE
Boston College loses at Florida State on Day 24 by 20 or more. It's 11-0, it's Tier C, and its schedule rates minus 1.94. Its best win is at Syracuse, a team that just lost at home to Utah. Florida State is 11-0 against real opposition. Boston College is 11-0 against people you've never heard of. One of those records is about to lose its innocence.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 22: Missouri at Alabama. Last week I said Alabama would win by double digits. After the LSU game I'm less sure, but I don't withdraw takes. I just watch them die. Also Iowa St. at Arizona, Texas at Florida, Fresno State at San Diego State, Florida State at Virginia and Seton Hall at Uconn.

Day 23: Illinois at Ohio St., two unbeaten Big 10 teams, for my Big 10 projection. Also Florida at Missouri, Utah St. at San Diego State, Butler at Seton Hall and Valparaiso at Southern Illinois.

Day 24: Boston College at Florida State, Seton Hall at Georgetown, Ohio St. at Michigan St. and Kansas State at Iowa St.

The scoreboard after seven weeks: Duke over Kentucky, landed and still being celebrated. Illinois in the Big 10, retired. Alabama not winning the SEC, deceased. Tennessee St. unbeaten, deceased. Duke over San Diego State, deceased by one point. Inna lillahi. I'm running out of black suits.

season-3.headline: Week 8: Arizona Takes the No. 1 Overall, San Diego State Loses Twice at Home, and Two Hot Takes Actually Land
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ, where for the first time this season I'm reporting a hot take that landed on schedule. Last week I said Alabama would beat Missouri by double digits and that Missouri would lose twice in its first three SEC games. Alabama won 84-74. Missouri then lost 75-73 at home to Florida. Two predictions, two hits. I'd like a moment of silence for all the hot takes that died so these two could live.

The Boston College take, on the other hand: I said Florida State would win by 20 or more. It won 92-88. Right winner, wrong postcode. I'll take a half point and a polite cough.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
San Diego State lost two home games in two days. Arizona beat three good teams by an average of 26 points. Seton Hall's three games in three days ended 1-2. Navy lost twice to a 4-12 Lehigh team and then to Army. Five teams are still unbeaten, and four of them are on the top line.

ARIZONA IS THE NO. 1 OVERALL SEED
Remember Week 1? Arizona lost at Oakland and I wrote that it was "the team in a horror film that walks into the basement." It's 13-1 now, it's won 13 straight, and this week it beat Iowa St. 85-63, Baylor 97-72 and won 83-51 at West Virginia. Three top-50 teams, three blowouts, three days. Its rating jumped 5.0 points to second in the country, and it's first on the Board at 42.56. Nobody else is above 39.

So Arizona is the No. 1 overall seed in the East. The team that walked into the basement turned out to own the house.

THE TOP LINE
Arizona, Ohio St. (South), Florida State (West) and Kansas (Midwest).

Ohio St. beat Illinois and won at Michigan St. this week. Florida State and Kansas are 14-0 too. Two Big 12 teams on the top line, and the schedule never puts them in the same building. The Big 12 tournament will have to do it.

Gonzaga drops to a 2 despite being 13-0. Here's why, and I know how it sounds. Gonzaga has zero wins over top-25 teams. Its best win is over a BYU team rated 29th. Kansas, Ohio St. and Florida State each have two top-25 wins, Arizona has three, and all four have played tougher schedules. It's like being the best player at a five-a-side game in your back garden.

SAN DIEGO STATE: THE FALL
Two editions ago San Diego State was rated 34.74, and in Week 5 I said it was in its own postcode. This week it lost 80-74 at home to Fresno State, then 77-69 at home to Utah St. It was expected to win those games by 17.5 and 17.0 points. Its rating fell 4.4 points to seventh. It's 2-2 in the Mountain West, and both Fresno State and Utah St. are ahead of it in the standings.

It's a 2 seed, and I'm still projecting it to win the Mountain West tournament, because it's still the best team in that league by six rating points. But "best team in the league" and "two home losses in two days" are rarely in the same sentence. Fresno State is a 5. Utah St., 4-0 in the league, is a 4.

SETON HALL: THE JOKE CONTINUES
Last week I said that if Seton Hall won all three games in three days, I'd stop making this joke. Seton Hall lost 81-66 at Uconn, beat Butler by 36, then lost 74-50 at Georgetown. It's 10-4. It's rated fourth in the country. It has still never beaten a top-25 team.

The joke stays. Georgetown takes the Big East projection. It's 10-2, up 2.9 rating points to tenth, it won 89-77 at Villanova, and it beat the team that's supposedly the fourth-best in the country by 24. Georgetown is a 3 seed, and so is Seton Hall, which is generous to Seton Hall and I'll hear no complaints from Seton Hall about it.

TENNESSEE ST. IS A 4 SEED
Under the commissioner's new rule, mid-major champions get seeded on merit, and Tennessee St.'s merit is enormous. It's 13-1, rated 17th, 16th on the Board, and it beat Tennessee Tech 103-43 this week. It goes from an 8 to a 4. Two weeks ago it was a 12 seed on a technicality. Now Arizona might have to play it in the Sweet 16. I'd pay to watch Arizona's faces during the anthem.

MOVERS
Texas goes from a 3 to a 2 after winning 74-59 at Florida.

Illinois drops from a 4 to a 6. It lost 74-73 at Iowa and then at Ohio St. Miami drops from a 4 to a 6 after losing at Virginia Tech. Kansas State drops from an 8 to a 10 after losing 60-55 at a 4-10 Cincinnati team.

VCU drops from a 4 to an 8. It lost 83-69 at Fordham, a game it was expected to win by 25.5. Fordham also won at Dayton this week. Fordham is 6-8. Fordham is the most dangerous 6-8 team in America and possibly the only one.

LSU beat Alabama last week and was the story of the season. This week it lost to Vanderbilt by 21 and to Missouri 84-40. It drops from an 11 to a 14. Forty-four points. LSU went from beating the champion to losing by more than its own score, in four days.

THE BUBBLE
Out: Mississippi State and Navy. Mississippi State is 0-4 in the SEC and lost 68-52 at Auburn, a 2-12 team, in a game it was expected to win by 26.8. Navy was my Patriot champion since Week 1. This week it lost 67-62 and 72-49 to Lehigh, a 4-12 team, and 57-48 at Army, a 3-13 team. Its rating fell 6.2 points, from 78th to 140th. I gave Navy a free pass in Week 1 for losing to Columbia. I've now revoked it, laminated the revocation and framed it next to the Kentucky one.

In: Michigan, which is 8-6 and has beaten Purdue and won at Penn State by 20.

Last four in: Louisiana against Florida Atlantic, and Providence against Michigan.

Louisiana is 12-2, 4-0 in the Sun Belt, and it hosts Marshall, my Sun Belt champion, on Day 27. Florida Atlantic is 8-5 and lost by 26 at Memphis this week, which hurts, but it still has no bad losses. Providence lost twice to Butler and then won two road games. Michigan is the most improbable at-large in the field: a Tier S team rated 55th that was out of the field for the last two weeks, now back on the strength of having stopped losing to everyone.

First four out: Kentucky, Dayton, Ole Miss, Coastal Carolina. Next four out: New Mexico, Mississippi State, Pepperdine, Washington State. Kentucky is 1-3 in the SEC, and at this point Kentucky is my most loyal reader. It's been first four out two weeks running.

AUTOMATIC BIDS
Four change. Georgetown takes the Big East. American takes the Patriot, 4-0 in the league after beating Holy Cross twice. Ball State takes the MAC after beating Ohio and starting 4-0. Cal State Northridge takes the Big West back, having won 69-68 at Hawaii. That's the third Big West change in three weeks, so I've stopped telling Hawaii anything in case it gets its hopes up.

PATTERNS
Tier S teams went 50-25 this week. That's 67 percent, by some distance their worst week of the season. Sixty-two games were decided by three points or fewer, a new high, and 12 went to overtime.

HOT TAKE
Texas beats Alabama on Day 26, and Texas wins the SEC. Alabama has the champion's crown and the better rating, but Texas is 4-0 in the league, it's won at Florida and at Texas Tech, and its only loss all season was to San Diego State on a neutral floor. I've spent eight weeks underrating Texas because it didn't play anyone in November. It's playing people now.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 25: Kansas at Iowa St., Kansas State at Arizona and San Diego State at San Jose State. San Diego State needs a road win before it forgets how.

Day 26: Texas at Alabama, Florida State at Duke, San Diego State at Fresno State, and Iowa St. at Kansas, the rematch, a day later. North Carolina at Miami too.

Day 27: Kansas at West Virginia, Nebraska at Illinois and Marshall against Louisiana for first place in the Sun Belt.

Day 28: Baylor at Kansas. Kansas plays Iowa St. twice and Baylor in four days. If it's still unbeaten after that, it's the No. 1 overall.

The scoreboard: Duke over Kentucky, landed. Alabama over Missouri by double digits, landed. Missouri losing two of three, landed. Boston College losing, landed, sort of. Everything else, deceased. That's three and a half hits. Alhamdulillah. I'm finally on a run.

season-3.headline: Week 9: Texas Wins at Alabama, Kansas Loses Three in Three Days, and the First Four Moves Where It Belongs
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Last week's hot take: Texas beats Alabama on Day 26 and wins the SEC. Texas won 73-72, at Alabama. By one point. I lost the Duke take by one point and won this one by one point, so the universe and I are square, and I'd like to keep it that way.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Kansas lost three games in three days. Missouri lost three games in three days, two of them to teams outside the top 100. Miami lost at home to a 5-12 Notre Dame team by 17. Three teams are still unbeaten: Florida State, Gonzaga and Ohio St. And the commissioner has changed the rules of the First Four, which means I get to explain a new system before anyone can tell me it's wrong.

THE NEW FIRST FOUR
Here's the old way. The last four at-large teams play in Dayton for two 11 seeds, and the four weakest conference champions play for two 16 seeds. That works in a normal year. This isn't a normal year. Two weeks ago the commissioner pointed out that strong small-conference champions should be seeded where they belong, and that pushed at-large teams down to the 12, 13 and 14 lines. Which left me with an absurd bracket: the four worst at-large teams in the field were 11 seeds, sitting above at-large teams I rated better than them.

So here's the new rule, and I'm calling it the Dayton Rule. A First Four game is one slot in the bracket, like any other. It gets seeded where its two teams belong on the S-curve, at the average of the pair. The winner inherits that seed.

In a normal year, that puts the last four at-large teams around the 11 or 12 line, exactly where they always were. This year it puts them on the 14 line, because California Baptist is 20-3, Oakland is 14-2, Denver is 14-3 and Louisiana is 14-3, and Kentucky and Michigan are 11-6 and 10-6. If you're one of the last four teams into the field, you play an extra game and you face a 3 seed. That's not a punishment. That's an accurate description of your season.

The site's own field builder now works the same way, so when the commissioner builds the real bracket on Selection Sunday, the First Four games will land where their teams fit, not on a line chosen in 2011.

THE TOP LINE
Arizona (East), Florida State (South), Ohio St. (West) and Gonzaga (Midwest).

Arizona is still the No. 1 overall seed: 16-1, 7-0 in the Big 12, and first on the Board at 42.71. It beat Kansas State 86-84 in overtime, then West Virginia by 26, then won 96-76 at Texas Tech. With Kansas melting, Arizona also takes the Big 12 projection, the fourth time it has changed hands this season. I've stopped apologising for it.

Florida State is 17-0 and won at Virginia Tech, at Duke and at NC State, all in three days. The Duke game finished 94-60. Gonzaga and Ohio St. are 16-0 and have stopped being tested by anyone in their leagues.

Kansas falls from a 1 seed to a 3. Last week I said that if Kansas survived Iowa St. twice and Baylor, it'd be the No. 1 overall. It never got to Baylor in one piece: it lost 80-77 at Iowa St., then 75-56 at home to Iowa St., then 77-72 in overtime at West Virginia. Three losses in three days, after 14 straight wins. That's not a slump. That's a demolition with a press release.

Texas moves into the 2 line alongside Alabama, San Diego State and Seton Hall, and takes the SEC projection.

THE MISSOURI COLLAPSE
Two weeks ago Missouri was 11-0. It has now lost five of its last six. This week it lost at Kentucky, at Tennessee, a 5-12 team, and at Georgia. It's 2-5 in the SEC and its rating fell 4.8 points, the biggest drop of any top-25 team. It drops from a 3 to a 7. My Week 6 hot take called Missouri's unbeaten record "a sandcastle." The tide came in, and then it kept coming in, and now it's taking the furniture.

KENTUCKY, AT LAST
Kentucky, my most loyal reader, has spent two weeks as the first team out. This week it beat Missouri and Mississippi State before losing at Alabama. It's in. It's a 14 seed in a First Four game against Michigan, playing for the right to face a 3 seed. In Week 1 Kentucky was a freshly promoted Tier S team and a 6 seed. Now it's back in the field through the service entrance, holding the door for Michigan.

MOVERS
Arkansas jumps from a 9 to a 5. It's 16-1, up 3.7 rating points to 24th, and beat Texas A&M by 26 and Oklahoma by 34 this week. Arkansas has lost one game all season, to Vanderbilt. Nobody talks about Arkansas, which is exactly how Arkansas likes it.

Miami drops from a 6 to an 8. The 80-63 home loss to Notre Dame was the biggest upset of the week by a distance: Miami was expected to win by 32.4. Iowa St. went 2-1, beat Kansas twice, then lost 74-60 at a 6-11 Cincinnati team in a game it was expected to win by 26.8. It stays a 3 because two wins over Kansas count for more than one disaster in Cincinnati. Duke drops from an 8 to a 10 after losing at home to Stanford and by 34 to Florida State.

New Mexico State lost its unbeaten record, 65-54 at Delaware, an 8-9 team. It stays a 5. One bad loss doesn't erase sixteen wins, but it does stop the 30-for-30 documentary.

THE BUBBLE
Out: St. Louis, which lost at home to Saint Joseph's and then to Loyola (IL), a 6-10 team, in a game it was expected to win by 23.3.

In: Kentucky.

Last four in, both on the 14 line under the Dayton Rule: Kentucky against Michigan in the East, and Providence against Florida Atlantic in the Midwest. Michigan has won its last two and is 4-2 in the Big 10. Providence lost to Seton Hall by 26 but has no bad losses all season. Florida Atlantic is 5-1 in the American and also has no bad losses. All four are deeply average. Two of them will be playing a 3 seed in the first round, which is about right.

First four out: St. Louis, New Mexico, Marshall, Pepperdine. Next four out: Wofford, Arizona State, Richmond, Davidson.

AUTOMATIC BIDS
Six change. Texas takes the SEC, Arizona the Big 12. Dayton takes the A-10 after winning 94-60 at VCU. Louisiana takes the Sun Belt from Marshall. Marshall did beat Louisiana this week, but it also lost to Louisiana–Monroe and by 23 at South Alabama, and Louisiana is 6-1 in the league. Longwood takes the Big South at 4-0 after South Carolina Upstate lost at home to High Point by 15. Bellarmine takes the ASUN: it's 7-0 in the league and beat Queens, which has three bad losses.

PATTERNS
Seventy-five games this week were decided by three points or fewer, the most of the season by a mile, and 14 went to overtime. Tier A teams went 37-38. That's a losing record for the second-best tier in the league, which tells you how hard conference play is on the teams just below the elite. Home teams won 60.2 percent.

HOT TAKE
Utah St. beats San Diego State on Day 28, sweeps the season series and wins the Mountain West regular season, and I move the projection by next week. Utah St. is 6-0 in the league and already won at San Diego State. San Diego State is 4-2, rated higher, and has to go to Utah St. I've kept San Diego State as the Mountain West pick on talent for two weeks. Talent is lovely. Standings are louder.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 28: San Diego State at Utah St., Baylor at Kansas, Georgetown at Butler, Iowa St. at BYU and Texas at Ole Miss. Kansas needs a win before the rumours start.

Day 29: Iowa at Ohio St., Florida at Arkansas, Colorado at Iowa St., Butler at Uconn and Texas A&M at Missouri. Missouri at home against Texas A&M is the most important game of Missouri's season. That sentence would have been ridiculous three weeks ago.

The scoreboard: Duke over Kentucky, landed. Alabama over Missouri, landed. Missouri's collapse, landed and still landing. Texas over Alabama, landed. Next up, Utah St. over San Diego State. I'm on a heater. Mashallah, and please nobody touch anything.

season-3.headline: Week 10: Utah St. Sweeps San Diego State, Florida State and Arizona Stumble, and the AP Poll Finally Agrees With Me
season-3.body:
Good morning from Bracketology HQ. Last week's hot take: Utah St. beats San Diego State, sweeps the series and takes the Mountain West. Utah St. won 77-70, is 8-0 in the league, and takes the projection. That's two hot takes in a row and three of the last four. I'm not superstitious, but I've worn the same socks for nine days and I'm not changing them.

THE WEEK IN ONE BREATH
Ohio St. and Gonzaga are still unbeaten, and nobody else is pretending any more. Arizona beat UCF by 31 at home and then lost to UCF by 12 the next day, on the road. Florida State lost twice. Texas scored 48 points at Mississippi State and lost. Baylor lost three games and scored 41 against Arizona. And 83 games were decided by three points or fewer, the third straight week that number has set a season high. Conference play isn't producing basketball games. It's producing heart conditions.

THE TOP LINE, AND WHAT THE AP THINKS
Ohio St. is the No. 1 overall seed in the East. It's 19-0, won at UCLA by 22 and at Penn State by 20, and beat Iowa by 27 in between. Arizona goes South, Gonzaga West and Texas Midwest.

The commissioner's AP poll has the same top four: Ohio St., Gonzaga, Arizona, Texas. This is the first time all season the AP poll and I have agreed on anything, and I'd like it noted that it's the AP voters who came round to my view, not the other way round. I have no evidence for that.

But the AP poll is the realest ranking there is, so it deserves a proper read. Three things jump out.

First, the AP has Seton Hall 14th. I have it on the 3 line, ninth overall, because the ratings still think it's the fourth-best team in the country. The voters have looked at a team with zero wins over top-25 opponents and said, politely, no. They figured out Seton Hall about six weeks before I did, and I've been making the joke the whole time.

Second, the AP has Illinois seventh. I have it 15th, on the 4 line. Illinois is 17-2, but its last three wins came by 12 at Wisconsin, by 4 over UCLA and by 1 at Indiana. The AP is rewarding the record. I'm worried about the trend. We'll find out who's right on Day 33, when Michigan St. goes to Illinois.

Third, the AP dropped Florida State from second to ninth. I've dropped it from a 1 to a 2. We agree on the direction. We disagree on how far to throw it.

ARIZONA'S STRANGE WEEK
On Day 28 Arizona beat UCF 92-61 at home. On Day 29 it lost 69-57 at UCF, a 9-10 team, in a game it was expected to win by 30.0. On Day 30 it won 77-41 at Baylor. That's one team going from 31 up to 12 down to 36 up in 72 hours. Arizona keeps its 1 seed because the other two results were absurd in the good direction, but it's no longer the overall No. 1, and the UCF loss is the first bad loss on its résumé.

FLORIDA STATE COMES BACK TO EARTH
Florida State lost 75-60 at home to Syracuse, an 11-9 team, then 95-78 at Boston College. It drops from a 1 to a 2, and North Carolina, 18-1 and 9-0 in the ACC, takes the conference projection.

Boston College deserves its own paragraph. In Week 7 my hot take was that Florida State would beat it by 20. In Week 8, Florida State won by four. This week Boston College beat Florida State by 17. Boston College is 17-2, rated 28th, and a 7 seed. I'd like to retroactively change my Week 7 take to "Boston College is good," and I'd like nobody to check.

MISSOURI'S RESURRECTION
Last week Missouri had lost five of six and I compared it to a sandcastle with the tide coming in. This week it won at Vanderbilt, beat Texas A&M by 26 and beat Alabama 73-72. It goes from a 7 to a 4. The sandcastle survived, rebuilt itself and beat the defending champion. I don't know what to do with this team, and I suspect Missouri doesn't either.

Alabama stays a 2. It's 16-3 with three top-25 wins, tied for the most in the country. It also plays at Texas on Day 31, and that's for the SEC.

MOVERS
Baylor drops from a 6 to a 10. It lost at Kansas, then by 22 at Cincinnati, an 8-12 team, then by 36 at home to Arizona. It scored 41 points. Baylor was 7-0 and a 1 seed in Week 4. It's now 13-7, and the 1 seed version is a rumour.

Tennessee St. drops from a 5 to an 8 after losing 67-57 at Tennessee–Martin, an 8-12 team. Its rating fell 3.4 points, from 18th to 29th.

THE DAYTON RULE, WEEK TWO
Last week the at-large First Four games both landed on the 14 line. This week they've split, because the teams around them moved. St. Louis against Kentucky is on the 13 line in the South, and Michigan against Providence is on the 14 line in the West. That's the point of the rule: the games go where their teams belong, and their teams keep changing.

Kentucky is in the First Four for the second week running, and it should be grateful for that much. It lost at home to South Carolina and then 69-62 at Ole Miss. Ole Miss beat Kentucky head to head and takes a direct 12 seed. Kentucky, my most loyal reader, is still in the building, just in the queue for the side door.

St. Louis is back in the field after winning by 31 at St. Bonaventure and beating Fordham by 28, before losing by one at Dayton. Michigan lost at home to Washington, which nearly cost it its place, then won by 20 at Nebraska. Providence lost to Villanova by a point and then won by 32 at Xavier.

Out: Florida Atlantic, which lost at UAB and fell to 85th in the ratings.

First four out: New Mexico, Mississippi State, Arizona State, Richmond. Mississippi State beat Texas this week, but it has four bad losses. A win over the 1 seed and four losses to teams outside the top 100 is a résumé that argues with itself. Next four out: Louisiana Tech, Florida Atlantic, Wofford, NC State.

AUTOMATIC BIDS
Six change. North Carolina takes the ACC and Utah St. takes the Mountain West, covered above. Marshall takes the Sun Belt back after Louisiana lost at Coastal Carolina and at home to an 8-11 Texas State team. South Dakota takes the Summit: it's 7-0 in the league and won 90-76 at Denver, my pick. Queens takes the ASUN back from Bellarmine after beating it and rising 3.0 rating points to 40th. South Carolina Upstate takes the Big South after Longwood lost by 19 at Charleston Southern. That's my fifth Big South change of the season. At this point I'd like the Big South to just tell me in advance.

PATTERNS
Eighty-three one-possession games. Home teams won 61.8 percent, the best of the season. Scoring fell to 66.4 points per team, the lowest of the season. Tighter, slower, more home-sided. Every week of conference play has added up to the same thing: the gap between good and very good is shrinking, and the gap between home and away is growing.

HOT TAKE
North Carolina is a 1 seed by Week 12. It's 18-1, 9-0 in the ACC, and rated 12th, which undersells it. It's won 18 straight since losing at New Orleans in Week 1. Boston College visits on Day 33, and if North Carolina wins that, it's the clear ACC favourite with Florida State fading. The AP has it eighth. I have it 12th. In two weeks, we'll both be wrong in the other direction.

WHAT TO WATCH
Day 31: Alabama at Texas for the SEC lead, Colorado at Kansas and Arkansas at Florida.

Day 32: Arizona at Colorado, Chattanooga at East Tennessee State with both unbeaten in the SoCon, Illinois at Oregon, Villanova at Seton Hall and San Jose State at Fresno State.

Day 33: Ohio St. at Nebraska, Boston College at North Carolina, Michigan St. at Illinois, Colorado at Arizona and San Jose State at San Diego State.

The scoreboard: Duke over Kentucky, Alabama over Missouri, Missouri's collapse, Texas over Alabama and Utah St. over San Diego State. Five landed. Missouri's collapse has since been reversed on appeal, so call it four and a half. Alhamdulillah, the socks stay on.
